Foreword
______________________________
TLDR
	The key differences between Rotten Core's history and ours boil down to 3 points:
		1. Vladimir Lenin was succeeded by a triumvirate, rather than by Stalin. The USSR was much closer to its founding ideals, and the Eastern Bloc was much more unified - the Sino-Soviet split never happened, for example. But by 1994, the bureaucracy founded by Stalin's supporters took over across the Eastern bloc. They ruled for 15 years, when in 2009 the entire bloc collapsed into brutal civil war - imagine the Yugoslav wars, but covering nearly all of Eurasia.
		2. Huey Long, the founder of modern American populism, survived his 1935 assassination, and went on to become the puppetmaster of the American government throughout the Second World War. However, the development of a corrupt oligarchy from his dirty tricks made him realise it was all for nothing, and he killed himself in 1946, his successor being ousted in the '48 elections by Douglas MacArthur and his clique, leading to a Cold War America even more openly corporatocratic than OTL (basically, imagine Reagan being about as far left as things get.)
		3. The British Empire fell violently, as anti-independence crackdowns triggered mass revolts. Canada was annexed by the US; Australasia (a police state formed from Australia and New Zealand) became a militaristic hegemon; South Africa initially joined the Axis, and later, backed by the USA, maintained apartheid well into the 2010s; and the Raj became taken over by the Azad Hind movement, leading to oppression, rebellion, and more oppression in its Muslim and Sikh provinces. Ireland, however, remained under British rule; in 2002, a crackdown in Derry was so brutal, it earned the nickname 'The Bogside War.' Thanks to the "Imperial Boomerang," the British domestic government is de-facto anocratic, with a rigged two-party system and a marginalised left wing, similar to the USA.
	
	Aside from all of this, many smaller things happened across the world - you can read the Primer to check on the 'modern day,' or just read ahead.

	On behalf of all of us, I hope you enjoy this story, and without further ado...
	WELCOME TO THE ROTTING WORLD.

		SCENE
			The morning sun dragged itself up from the horizon, shining softly over Geneva. Cold autumnal winds swept through the World City, scattering orange leaves like glitter on a child's drawing. Zeppelins floated through the skies, while jetplanes crisscrossed above them. Down below, the people moved like ants.
			Zhao looked both ways at the small road, and crossed quickly. He pulled his coat's hem, trying to keep some warmth.
			He felt like someone was watching him. But then, he always did.
			Ahead, a large, gleaming building of glass and steel - the World Health Organisation's headquarters. Or, as he thought of it: work.
			"Good morning, Eva." he nodded as he entered.
			"Good morning, Dr. Zhao!"
			The barrier slid open, and he passed through, glancing over his shoulder.
			From the outside, a noise bled in - some kind of engine running, or an abnormal wind effect. Before he could place it, a voice called out.
			"Morning, Zhao." an older, stern-faced man in a sharp suit nodded.
			"Ah, Dr. Ibekwe. Did you get those reports I sent you?"
			"I did. I must say... I thought the xeno-grehlin would've worked."
			A quiet sigh, before Ibekwe spoke again. "Back to the drawing board, I suppose."
			"I'll talk to the Director. Maybe we can--"
			"NOBODY FUCKIN' MOVE!"
			Gunshots. Lots of them.
			Shattering glass. Screaming.
			"RUN!" Zhao roared. Ibekwe froze, in blind panic.
			Zhao yanked open a door, and shoved Ibekwe through. He went to follow--
			*BANG!*
			At first, it didn't hurt. His heartbeat quickened as his eyes shot downwards. The bullet slammed into his knee, buckling it.
			Then, the pain hit. A scream ripped out of his throat, as he forced himself to see his assailant.
			"Please, I'm begging you--"
			He was answered by a rifle's stock crashing into his temple. His eyes rolled back as his conscious mind lulled.
			"Him, too." his attacker barked. 
			The rough hands of another gunman wrapped around Ibekwe's wrists.
			They dragged their prizes out to the front - where a black helicopter hovered lowly.
			Captives were thrown aboard, as Zhao was hauled in.
			As the chopper took off, the lead gunman put his fingers to his ear.
			"Command, this is Delta Five-One. Package secure."
			The engines screamed as their afterburners kicked in, and the chopper tore on through the skies.

			The room was dark. An imposing man, with greying hair and a cropped beard, was illuminated by a blue screen that flickered into white. Ink-black veins jutted and tore down his cheeks, like running mascara. A nexus of these clustered around his eyes, whose steel irises glimmered in the shadows.
			"Gentlemen." he began. He spoke with a Virginian accent - and at once sounded like honey and sulphur. "Thank you for attending."
			"Commandant." an implacable voice growled from the speakers. "You have a lot of nerve."
			"Enough. What's done is done." cut in a second voice. An older, upper-class accent was palpable, even through the modulation. "I have spoken with our friends in Geneva - no further action will be taken."
			"The operation was a success." the Commandant protested.
			"Oh it was, was it?" the first voice scowled.
			"To an extent." the second added. "The... erratic nature of the attack can be worked to our advantage. Federal Police will butt heads with UN Security, and Interpol will be completely ineffective. Switzerland's tradition of direct democracy has always limited our influence... By provoking public fear, we can herd the sheep into our pens."
			"And the WHO?"
			"Placated. We've pinned the attack on the Romand Citizen's Army. What matters now is that we have Dr. Zhao again. Now he must be reminded of his... obligations."
			"Oh, he will be reminded alright... I can *assure* you of that, sir." the Commandant scowled.
			"Good. Now... continue your report."
			"Gladly, sir." the Commandant nodded. "Operations in the East have progressed smoothly. The Reds are on the back foot."
			"Excellent." the first voice audibly grinned. "Our associates in America should be pleased. Lord Oxford, how fare our proxies in the third world?"
			"Quite well, quite well." the aristocrat replied. "Western backing of the Somali coup has opened up the nation's oil reserves to our backers, and by extension, us. How about on your front, Claus?"
			"I've been keeping an eye on Renard, as requested. He's been in contact with Neumann."
			"Damn fool. You almost have to admire the balls on him." Oxford audibly grinned.
			"And how about your group, Commandant?"
			"We work ever closer to the Final Victory, sir."
			"Indeed, indeed." Claus replied dismissively.
			"Don't forget who pays your wages, Commandant." Oxford added hastily. "Your... 'ideological inflexibilities' had better not impair our operations."
			"Of course not, sir." the Commandant nodded, his lip curling silently.
			"Commandant?" Claus chimed in. A hint of glee cut through the modulation.
			"Yes, sir?"
			"You are hereby ordered to cease all activities regarding the Progeny investigation. Just bring Zhao back to Drackhill, and restart production. The 'children' are off-limits."
			"Agreed." Oxford added. "The last thing we need is to provoke Neumann even further. Geneva was bad enough..."
			"...Sir." the Commandant reluctantly growled. He cut off the call, and dialed a second number.
			"Commandant!" a jovial voice exclaimed. "How did the meeting with the Board go, sir?"
			"Need-to-know basis, Morland."
			"That badly, eh?"
			The Commandant didn't reply. Instead, he called another number.
			"Commandant, sir. Mr. Morland, sir."
			"Five-One." the Commandant began. "Is everything in place?"
			"Yes, sir." the soldier audibly nodded. "Drackhill ETA is 45 Mikes. My men on the ground have moved into the field lab."
			The Commandant stroked the hairs on his chin, before taking a deep breath.
			"And the boy?"
			"We're ready to grab him, sir."
			The Commandant grinned savagely. "I'll do it. I'll meet you at the Fenrir site."
			"As you wish, sir."
			"Morland - you have your orders," he continued. "Damn the board to hell, Progeny will be mine. And soon, you shall have more supply than you can dream of."
			"Excellent, sir." Morland gleefully replied. "Hail Victory."
			"Hail Victory, sir."
			"Hail Victory." the Commandant nodded. He switched off his computer, and lit a cigar. He took a long drag, and smiled devilishly.

		SCENE
			It was the 9th of October, 2015. A crisp, cold Friday morning.
			The sun shone in through the curtainless window, illuminating a 2-bed apartment. In one room laid a young man, with scruffy, dark-blonde hair. Strands fell across his forehead in no particular order, as though sleep itself had styled them, while a faint ginger stubble shadowed his jaw.
			Connor Barrett.
			His phone, plugged into a charger on the floor and resting on the bedside table, began to hum a pleasant-sounding tune.
			Connor groaned, and sat up, pulling the blanket off of him. He turned off the alarm, looked down at his pillow, and seriously considered saying "Fuck it," and staying home.
			Nevertheless, he forced himself to rise. He stretched out, and it felt like every joint in his body clicked at once. In truth, just his shoulders and knees.
			He leant forward, stretching out his back and touching his toes.
			"Fuck me..." he muttered, before shuffling like a zombie towards the kitchen space, and making himself a coffee. His accent had a funny quality - it was never sure where it was from. He sounded like a local, but had strong Irish influences as well. As for his tone, it was flat - intonations were largely neutral, as though he put far more stock into words than their presentation.
			He sipped from the cup, and allowed the bitter taste to snap him into reality. He walked to the window and considered a cigarette, then shook his head. He opened it and leant out, breathing in through the nose to absorb the city's smell.
			Drackhill. Once a major industrial hub, set to be the economic capital of the south-west. The city sat comfortably in the Drackhill Valley, nestled between Dartmoor and the coast. Connor's flat was on the western side of Drackhill - a poor, neglected township called Redbridge.
			He craned his head, and looked across the river. He could see the old, dilapidated industrial district of Belson. He saw the wealthy, uptight centre of Caldermouth. He looked out, and saw the rolling hills and moors of Blackmarsh. On the horizon, he could just about make out the nearby town of Wickermast. Finally, he finished this little exercise by climbing his eyes up the great hill in the centre of the city - Wyrmrock. The city's ancient namesake, from an old tale of dragons and trolls. He cracked a slight grin, watching two airships pass each other by.
			He sniffed at his armpit, and grimaced, before heading into the bathroom, stripping, and hopping into the shower.
			Hopping wasn't hyperbole - fully awake, he vaulted the bathtub's side and used his toes to soften his descent. He grinned at his own lameness.
			The hot--well, lukewarm--water flowed over his skin, washing away the sweat and the stink. He reached for the shower gel, and focused on the important bits - hair, armpits, groin. He vigorously rubbed a spot on his arm, only for the sleep-dust in his eyes to clear, and he realised it was just his freckles. He chuckled.
			He looked at his reflection in the mirror. His steel-grey eyes caught the flickering ceiling light. He pulled his cheek with his hand, inspecting his stubble. He shrugged, content with its length, and brushed his hair.
			Clean now, he buffeted himself with a towel, only to hear a banging on the door.
			"Oi, dickhead! Hurry up."
			He grinned, threw on some pants and a shirt, and opened the door to his flatmate and foster-sister.
			"About time." she snarked. Her name was Amelia Zhao - and she'd kick you in the groin if you called her that. Everyone called her Amy.
			Her hair was almost the platonic ideal of a punk rocker's style - dyed jet-black, with bright red tips bouncing in the draft. A fringe neatly framed her hazel eyes, and the right side had been cropped into a short undercut, while the rest hung freely from her head. A collage of tattoos covered her arms, some crudely self-applied, some professional.
			"Morning, twat." Connor chirped back nonchalantly.
			"Yeah, no time for small talk. Need a piss." she chuckled, pushing past him and closing the door.
			"Love you too." he grinned, heading to his room to finish dressing himself.
			He checked his rota. He saw he'd be on shift with Trey, and let out a silent cheer. Sufficiently motivated, he pulled his jacket over him, slipped on his baseball cap, and left the flat.

			It was a normal day for Riverside Repairs. The scent of oil and old coffee hung in the air. A car with a broken radio was positioned in the repair bay, the news broadcast being spat out in garbled syllables.
			"--paratist forces--eiged the capital--eaving thousands woun--"
			Connor climbed into the car and gave the radio a whack. A whirring noise came over the speaker. He opened the glovebox, and plugged in a small device. The tone shifted from high, to low, to higher, to lower. Then, a click. Another click.
			"Connor? You got it yet?" Trey called out, peeking his head from the open bonnet. He was a lean, muscular guy with dark skin, brown eyes, and a chinstrap beard framing his grin. His dreads were tied up in a high ponytail, the fade at the sides catching the light when he moved. A couple of locks were too short to be tied up, and instead dangled freely at his temples. He was wearing mechanic's overalls, which were almost spotless. His voice was the platonic ideal of a working-class English boy - he had strong Cockney and Estuary influences, but with enough Devon elements to make it his own.
			"Nearly." Connor replied. He fiddled with his device, and then - a loud beep.
			"Try it now." he called out. Trey grinned, and re-attached the jumper leads to the car's battery.
			Connor turned the keys into the ignition, and a smooth start preceded a sigh of relief.
			The newscaster continued to report on the Eurasian Wars in the background, this time free of glitch and garble.
			Connor cleared his throat. "There you go, Ms. Carrister - the radio should be sorted now."
			"If you have any problems miss, please don't hesitate to call us back." Trey added.
			"Thank you so much, darling!" the woman smiled. "And be rest assured, I'll be back - just to see your handsome faces!"
			Trey stifled a cringe and waved her off. He turned to Connor, now showing open disgust.
			"If that was a bloke, and I was a woman, that'd be creepy, yeah? So how come that's acceptable?"
			Connor blinked slowly. "Ooh, this is one of those things where we're mad at the hypocrisy, not the actual act, isn't it?"
			Trey tried to be angry, yet couldn't help but chuckle. "Fuck you!" he laughed. "Still creepy though."
			The boys began to close up. Once finished, they changed out of their overalls. Trey released his hair from its man-bun, allowing his undercut dreadlocks to flop down by his ears.
			Connor turned to him. "You out tonight?"
			"Yeah man!" Trey smiled. "You coming?"
			"Nah, I'm gonna stay in tonight. You know how it is... Noise, people, *stink...*"
			"No worries bro - I'll see you Sunday morning?"
			"Afternoon - I switched shifts with Jake." Connor replied.
			Trey put on a look of horror. "...you mean I have to open with *Jake?*"
			"He's not that bad." Connor said, but couldn't lie convincingly enough. "Okay, fine, he is. But at least I'll see you in the afternoon."
			"Bring coffee... or drugs." Trey groaned.
			Connor chuckled. "You whinge about opening with Jake, but you wonder why I don't wanna come out."
			Trey grinned in response. "Fair point. I'll quit whinging if you come out."
			Connor rolled his eyes, and nodded.

			Inside, several men with similar uniforms and black-veined eyes were variously loading or unloading trucks with medical equipment, weapons, restraints, and obscure devices and artefacts.

			The assailant finished firing, and grinned. Connor's eyes flashed bright, as he stumbled down to his knees.
			"Goodbye, Connor." he sighed, before drawing his pistol.
			Connor, undeterred, gripped the barrel and squeezed. The barrel bent around his fingers. His gunman pulled the trigger, and the gun exploded in their hands.
			"FUCK!" he barked, clutching it as it bled. The crumbling pillars holding the barn finally gave way, and the whole burning building came crashing down.

			Emergency sirens blared from the roof of the fire engine. As it pulled up outside the blazing inferno formerly known as a dairy barn, its crew donned protective gear.
			"Alright, team - given the intensity of the fire, we can safely assume some high-grade accelerant was in place here. Thankfully, its isolation and the recent bloody rainstorm means we can keep it under control."
			One man raised his hand - the leader gestured affirmatively.
			"Cops been called yet?"
			"They said they'll get here soon enough. I assume this is either arson or a drug den, so they'll wanna do a look-over. Caller was a dog-walker who heard the explosion - according to the plods, this lot is owned by some random holding company, so we're suspecting criminal involvement. Tread carefully, and get this fire out."
			The firemen started hosing down the wreckage. After clearing the perimeter, they moved inwards.
			One, a young recruit, approached a heap of ash, dirt, and debris, hosing it down. Then, he nearly jumped out of his skin, as a horrifically burned hand pushed out of the detritus.
			"Shit!" he gasped. "Sir! Got a body here!"
			The hand pushed out further, revealing the full arm, before pulling the rest of the body out.
			A sight none could forget.
			A horribly burned man. Emaciated, almost skeletal. Hairless, skin charred and bloody, wearing nothing more than blackened tattered rags.
			"He's alive! Holy fuck!" the recruit shrieked.
			The leader rushed over.
			"Hey! It's okay! We're here to help!" he said, his face pale as a ghost.
			The burned man stepped forward, and gripped the leader, raising him up by the neck. He choked and spat, while his men screamed and cowered.
			His eyes flashed red once more, before fading. Connor dropped the fireman, and instinctively sprinted away.
			"What the fuck was that?!" the recruit asked, horrified.
			The leader choked, catching his breath.

		SCENE
			Another eon - or a minute - passed. Flashes once again rushed through Connor's mind.
			Finally, he awoke in a dark alleyway, in the pouring rain. He had just finished eating a live rat with his bare hands.
			He puked up blood, fur, meat, and bile.

			He didn't know who he was.

			But at least one victory - that was definitely *his* face.
			"I'm still me." he sighed in relief.
			The hairs on his neck itched. He looked around, and spotted in the distance - a long way away, and in the pouring rain, but yet, he could see it as if it were up close - it was a man in Patriot leathers. One of Slater's goons.
			Belson. He was in the Belson district. Skinhead territory. It wasn't far from home - an hour's walk, give-or-take. He could tell his location like he was a homing pigeon.
			He tried to sneak away, but - no. The man confidently sauntered towards him.
			"Oi, oi! The fuck are you doin' in our patch, boy?!" he spat.
			Connor prepared a stance, despite his aches and weakness. The man swung for Connor, and he ducked, then prepared an uppercut to the chin.
			He felt a surge of energy coursing through his limbs, a heat building in his chest, and his fist connected with the man's jaw.
			As he hit, he closed his eyes. He heard a massive, deep, booming sound, as though an explosive force ripped through the air.

			Holy shit.
			What the fuck.
			What the FUCK?!

			Blood.
			Blood everywhere.
			What?
			What?!
			WHAT?!

			The now-headless man stumbled backwards. His hands reached towards his neck-stump, and he fell down to the ground.
			Moments later, a sickening 'THWACK' sound pierced the air, as the man's head landed on the ground.
			For a moment, Connor stood frozen, unable to process what he'd just done. Then, the act hit him like a wave of nausea.
			His stomach turned, and bile rose up his throat as he stared at the lifeless body. His hands trembled, slick with blood, and he felt a cold dread seep into his bones.
			He ran as fast as he could. He finally came to a stop outside an alleyway. He vomited a bright yellow bile, and crawled into the alleyway.

			"Fuck..." he groaned, feeling pressure mounting under his skin - like something was going to burst out of it.
			His vision blurred and twisted. He looked back into the water, and saw the world go greyscale. And his eyes - they were almost glowing.
			Not almost. Bright enough to cast streaks across the water, like a lens flare. And the veins around his eyes - normally imperceptible - turned ink-black.
			"Gah..." he spat, blood and bile launching from his mouth. He clutched his head, and groaned in agony.
			The pressure was unbearable. It was like something inside him was trying to break free. His pulse quickened as the sensation intensified. He couldn't breathe, couldn't think - he only felt the agony of his own body betraying him.
			"Fuck... FUUUCK!" he screamed.
			For a moment, every nerve in his body seared in agony. But then... a black, tarry substance forced itself out from his skin, encasing him in it. And then it hardened, forming an exoskeletal bodysuit that covered him from head to toe. It hadened, then calfified, becoming a chitinous exoskeleton. Claws cut out from his hands, as he fell down to his knees.
			He looked back into the water, and under the exoskeleton, went even paler than before. His eyes blazed crimson.
			He felt a pounding in his chest - in his torso.
			Not *a* pounding. *Two* poundings.
			He felt his chest, and quickly confirmed - two heartbeats. Twin hearts.
			And as quickly as it had formed, the substance liquefied once more, and forced itself back down through his pores, leaving him wearing nothing but rags once more. Finally, mercifully, he collapsed.

		Connor returns
		______________________________
		SCENE
			Back home, Connor was in his bathroom, freshening up. He looked at his reflection. He gently, gingerly placed his hand on the mirror, and sighed deeply.
			He then stared deeply into his eyes, like he was focusing. He looked closer and closer - trying to hunt for abnormalities.
			Whatever he was, it wasn't quite human. Was he an alien? Was his body even his own?
			As he dissociated, the world turned greyscale once more. He gasped, noticing the change - feeling the warmth in his eyesockets again, and seeing the white glow form from them.
			Now focusing, and unburdened by the disorientation of his transformation, he took a closer look. The glow appeared limited to his irises - but it was bright. And his colour vision was gone.
			"Whoa..." he whispered, then gasped.
			The noises he made - he 'saw' the noise. The way the vibrations travelled through the air. The ripples coming from his mouth. Not in the mirror - he saw it come from the bottom of his field of vision, and cast outwards.
			He held his hand aloft, and snapped his fingers. Again, he 'saw' the sound come from it.
			"Super-vision?" he pondered aloud, mesmerised by the sight of his voice.
			He pulled out his phone, and took a photograph of his face. Then, he closed his eyes, and shook his head. When he reopened his eyelids, the world looked normal again. He clapped his hands, but could only hear the noise.
			Then, he looked at the photograph.
			The light from his eyes wasn't white, like he'd previously assumed. It was a terrifying red. They glowed with a demonic quality, as though fire might erupt from them. Surrounding his eyesockets, ink-black veins like those of the men who tortured him jutted around.
			He looked back in the mirror, and confirmed they'd returned to their previous steel-grey, and the veins had faded back into his skin.
			Eager to explore this strange new perception, he closed his eyes. He focused his listening - picking up even the smallest sounds. His own heartbeats. The sound of pipes throughout his tenement block. People talking, walking, arguing, or even snoring in their own homes. Noises a human couldn't ever hear. And they were deafening. His ears would put a bat to shame.
			He covered his ears, and the sound died down. Then, another idea.
			He applied this same 'tuning' to his vision, instead. His vision had gotten better since his rebirth, but now it was stronger than even that. He could see tiny micro-fractures in the mirror. The imperceptible ridges within the ceramic sink. He looked down at his hand, and saw the fingerprints and follicles and pores with complete precision. His eyes would put a falcon to shame.
			Then, he shifted from his eyes to his nose and mouth. He sniffed the air like a dog, and instinctively, he could recognise chemical signals he'd never even perceived. The toothpaste in the tube on his sink was at least 4 months old. As for the water in the plughole, he could tell it was soft. There was a stagnant stench coming from down the pipes.
			He'd done a remarkable job of cleaning away the biley vomit and blood in the bathroom, but the lingering micro-stains railed into his nostrils. He closed his eyes, and instinctively was able to tap where the stains were, simply locating them within his mental map by the proximity of their stink. His nose would put a wolf to shame.
			Tunable senses. Useless, though, if activating them would just overwhelm him.
			That's when it hit him.
			He re-activated the synesthetic 'super-vision,' and tuned his hearing back up. The noise was strong in his ears, but... bearable.
			Why wouldn't it be? He didn't need to 'hear' the sounds - now he could just 'see' them. Auditory input data was now being handled by optical processors. Like a load-balancing server.
			He looked around. Where he had heard the noises before, now he could see them. His hearing was strong enough that he could even see the heartbeats of the people on his floor.
			He looked at one heartbeat in particular - chosen at random - and focused his attention on it. Colour returned, but only on the rippling waves he could now see. They were bright red, like his eyes were now. He looked away, and looked back - the colour was still there, calling him.
			The perfect hunting system.
			He shook his head, turning it all off.
			"Hunting system?" he whispered aloud. "What the fuck am I thinking?"
			He turned it back on, but this time, with his eyes closed. Despite the thick skin covering his irises, he could still see rather clearly. He took a photograph of his face with his closed eyes, and then wandered around the flat.
			At first, he assumed he was simply seeing through the skin, such was the power of his vision. But it was more than that - despite his eyes being closed, his other super-senses were defined enough to help him visualise his surroundings in lieu of sight.
			Finally, he turned it all off, and looked at his photo. There was a faint red colouration on his eyelids, but nothing obviously supernatural.

			It had gotten dark now. To clear his mind, Connor went out for a jog - in the woodlands on the northern side of Wyrmrock.
			He ran and ran and ran, like a dog off the leash. He leapt over a stream, hitting the bank on the other side with a notable thud. Undaunted, he kept running. Miles passed, as he efforlessly looped around the woods.
			He came to a stop, and caught his breath in seconds. He crouched low, and looked out into the darkness.
			There, he saw it. A deer - a red deer, and a stag, to be precise. It had only just noticed him, and had gone still, waiting to see if he would chase.
			Something inside him pushed. Maybe his adrenaline, his super-senses, or just the thrill of his new-found powers. Maybe it was something darker. Inhuman. Feral.
			Maybe it was all of that.
			He smirked, and bolted.
			The stag bolted away, running as fast as its legs would take it. Ordinarily, no human could dream of keeping pace here. But Connor wasn't an ordinary human anymore...
			He gave chase, at points even running on all fours like an animal. His hearts raced, and his ears could sense the heartbeat of the deer. His super-vision activated automatically, and he saw the vibrations of his terrified prey. The heartbeat was, like before, highlighted in a blood-red glow, matching his demonic eyes. 
			This was pure thrill. An almost divine experience of animalism. Predator and prey.
			Connor slowed down, toying with his quarry, letting the chase go on for longer. He climbed a tree, and leapt in front of the stag, causing it to panic and turn frantically. Connor grinned with savage excitement, and continued the chase, like a cat playing with a mouse.
			He continued to pouce from tree to tree, instinctively knowing exactly where to grip, before leaping down and landing right on the stag.
			The poor creature yelped as its legs gave out, and without hesitation, Connor gripped its antlers and twisted. The stag shuddered, then went still.
			In seconds, Connor descended on its body. His teeth ripped past its hide and pulled out chunks of hot red meat. Blood sprayed from the entry wounds, as he pulled his kill apart and savagely devoured it.
			This was true life. An animal, and its food.
			He tore out another chunk, and felt the abysmal hunger that tormented him since his transformation fade away.
			Killing, and eating. That was what the Demon in his skull demanded.
			He swallowed, and went for another piece, before he finally realised what he had done.
			He looked down at his bloodied hands, then at the half-eaten stag, before standing, spitting out a chunk of meat and fur, and vomiting.
			Then, he stood, vomited again, and cried. Oh, how he cried.
			He howled in despair and sorrow, and clawed at his face.
			He cradled the dead stag, and tried to say "I'm sorry," but could only manage mumbles between sobs.
			It was a truly pitiful sight. A bloodied man, inelegantly blubbering over his kill.
			The awful headaches he'd been feeling had gone, but something worse gnawed at his very soul.
			Horror. Fear. Rage. Hate.
			Inhumanity.

		Deerstalker

		SCENE
			It had been a week since Connor's return. He was in the Singing Horse backrooms, working away while Tommy reviewed papers. His hair had started to grow back now, being long enough on top to brush it sideways again. He'd opted for a simple left-parting. His stubble had returned, and threatened to form a full beard.

			Connor paused. He hesitated.
			"No." he whispered. "Fuck this."

			"CONNOR!" Tommy barked, but he was long gone.
			"Shit." Pawel muttered. "Didn't know he could sprint like that." 
			
			Connor's breath was steady, despite the speed at which he ran. As he moved, he felt his pores erupt again - this time, covering his face in a balaclava. He took a moment to appreciate the utility, before heading on.
			He burst through the door without hesitation. The room went still for a moment before chaos erupted.
			The first man barely had time to react before Connor's fist slammed into his chest. The impact sent him flying backward, crashing into a table with a thud. The second man lunged, a knife glinting in his hand. Connor caught his wrist mid-swing, twisting it until the blade dropped. A single punch to the chin dropped the man to the floor, unconscious before he even landed.
			Connor raised his boot, ready to stomp on the man's head.
			The image of the man's head bursting apart like a squashed grape filled Connor's brains. He felt a deep disgust at how pleasing it looked.
			"NO!" Connor screamed back, stomping his foot next to the man's head, shaking the ground beneath. His breathing stabilised.
			While distracted, the third man lunged at Connor with a knife. It sank into his abdomen.
			For a split second, Connor expected to feel agony. But instead, all he felt was dull pain, rage, and... excitement?
			Another split second passed. The drumming ache in Connor's skull faded, as though the pain burned away the fog.
			Connor stepped forward. His fist shot out, catching the man under the chin. The crunch of teeth echoed through the room as the man's head snapped back, blood spraying from his mouth. He staggered, dazed.
			Connor took a milisecond to feel relief. He didn't kill him. He was still in control.
			With a quick, calculated motion, he slapped both of the man's ears. The force of the blow sent him crumpling to the ground, clutching his head and groaning in agony.
			Connor exhaled, steadying himself. The knife was still lodged in his abdomen, but the pain felt... different.
			It focused his mind. Grounded him. He closed his eyes for a moment, and let the agony wash over him.
			It was intoxicating, as though his pain and pleasure receptors had merged into one.
			It was a sickening, disgustingly satisfying sensation. Every moment the pain hummed into his flesh, he felt another spike of euphoria, as the awful migraines that plagued him since his transformation faded.
			"You... you saved--holy shit, your chest!" one person yelped.
			Connor glanced down, gripping the handle of the knife. He pulled it free with a single, fluid motion, blood staining the blade.
			The wound should have been gushing, but it... wasn't.
			The pain was already fading, melting into a strange, almost pleasant numbness. The wound itself... it wasn't deep.
			The skin around it was red and inflamed, but it began knitting itself back together before his eyes.
			"What am I?" he pondered, staring at the bloodied knife in his hand. He looked down at his attacker, and gripped the blade's handle.
			He felt his heartbeats slow--No, he felt time slow. His senses quickened.
			"No." he whispered. "No more." He threw the blade into the ground. It lodged itself hard in the floor.
			He clutched his wound, and sighed.
			The pain in his stomach faded, but there was a lingering ache deep inside.
			And not just the wound.
			It was something in him, something shifting, changing.
			And deep inside his skull, the dull, drumming agony returned, as though a demon in his brain was unhappy at the lack of slaughter.

			Without another word, he turned and jogged out of the centre, his steps steady despite the injury.
			By the time he reached the Singing Horse, the wound had closed entirely, leaving only a faint red mark.
			Soon, even that would be gone.
			Not a scar, not a trace.
			"Not a soul." he whispered. He un-formed the balaclava, and went into Tommy's office.
			"I told you not to!" Tommy snapped, his voice trembling with the kind of anger only fear for a loved one can bring.
			"And who knows who could have gotten hurt if I didnt?!" Connor countered.
			"...Still."
			"Still what?!"
			"It's dangerous, Connor! I promised - I *promised* Vince I wouldn't let you get hurt."
			Connor pulled up his shirt, revealing the faint mark.
			"I was stabbed, and that's all that's left. Not even gonna scar. And it barely hurt. You got any other enforcers like this? Can Pawel get stabbed and be fine?"
			Tommy slumped back into his chair.
			"Exactly." Connor folded his arms.
			"Connor..." Tommy began, "You... you can do things no one else can. Christ knows what'll happen to you if you get caught."
			"I could say the same for you."
			"They won't cut me up." Tommy replied, his face pale.
			"They've already cut me up. I'm fine."
			"You're not fine! Connor, please."
			"Tommy!" Connor shouted. "Tommy... You and Vince, you both taught me to fight against injustice. To help the helpless where I can. Well, now I *really* can."
			"But..." Tommy weakly protested.
			"What those bastards did to me..." Connor grimaced. "It was the worst thing that ever happened to me. But somehow, it made me like this. That mean I have a chance, Tommy. A chance to... to make it better. To make it mean something good."
			"... there's no stopping you, is there?" Tommy sighed wearily.
			"Would there be any stopping you?"
			"You're too much like your uncle." Tommy relented.
			"...Thank you." Connor smiled.
			"Make it count."
			Connor nodded, and left.
			"I can do anything." he thought to himself.
			"...No. Not anything." His mind flashed to the broken bones. The flying teeth. The dead man. The flayed stag.
			Who was he?
			Human?
			Monster?
			Both?
			Neither?

It budged, so he kicked again, knocking it free. He held it aloft, using it as a shield to charge the squadron, before bashing them in melee.

Then, he twisted his head, and a disgusting *SNAP* followed by blood-curdling screams marked the end of that man's contribution to the fight.

He swiftly spun around, pressing his back against the MRAP and holding his makeshift door-shield aloft. It made distinctive clanging sounds as bullets slammed into it or ricocheted off.
			Then, Connor raised the door into the air, and swung it into a soldier's head, making a satisfying *THUNK* noise as the man drifted into a deep sleep. Sparky gripped a soldier by his uniform, and threw him into the air. As he landed, the sound of bones popping out of their joints was overtaken by his cries of pain.
			Finally, a young, pimply soldier, who accidentally dropped his gun, tried desperately to crawl away. Sparky advanced, his eyes glowing deep blood-red. The soldier frantically kicked out, but Sparky grinned, baring his teeth.

He struggled to get close, but before long, he was in melee range. Then, he began swinging about like a madman.

Sparky, who had used this time to do some actual tactical thinking, prowled around and pounced in from their rear, making quick work of those Connor wasn't clobbering. Before long, the warriors were surrounded by broken and bleeding men. Connor de-formed the armour, and nearly collapsed, before steadying himself.

He picked up a chair, and launched it at one - then did the same to another. Their ribs made audible cracks as they collapsed.

He arrested and restrained the Defence Minister, then turned to the President.

And *I* can, for some reason, understand what you mean when you're barking and howling. And now we know that, when I'm speaking another language, you can still understand me."

Some people headed towards the mosque in groups, eager to begin the prayer. The vendor from before laid out his mat by the side of his stall, facing southeast towards Mecca. They went through the familiar motions of the Maghrib - the sunset prayer. Some made a show of being more pious - others were simply glad that after such a chaotic day, *this* part was still the same.

			The same chitinous, kevlar-like exoskeleton had encased him once more. And his eyes glowed bright red, lighting up the room. His claws - not hands, but claws - glinted in the light, like his fingers were knives.
			He took a deep breath, and ripped the covering from his face.
			"Amy, I--" he stammered.
			She didn't speak. Instead, she struggled to her feet, refusing to turn her back to him.
			"I... I'll let you go, just... p-please don't... don't hurt me..." she begged, tears streaming down her face.
			"Amy, I'm not gonna hurt you." he said as softly as he could. She made her way to her room, and rushed in, bolting the door.
			"Amy, wait!" he begged.
			"CONNOR!" Sparky barked, similarly encased in his battle-form. "We have to go!"
			Connor sighed, but nodded. The twin Werewolves headed out.

		Commandant Calls
		______________________________
		SCENE
			Across the city, Connor and Sparky perched atop an industrial unit. Sparky's fur flowed in the cold breeze, and their eyes flashed red as they scanned the fourth unit below.
			"Electromagnetic signals." Sparky noted. "Some electrical equipment in the walls."
			"Probably just wiring. Though, I'm not sure - that there looks like a radio receiver." Connor pointed.
			"Smells like WiFi." Sparky shrugged. "I doubt it's anything important. Can you get that plastic smell?"
			"Plastic? I thought it was oil." Connor tilted his head. "Well, this place is an industrial unit. Probably just old product."
			Sparky nodded, then his eyes darted. "See that?"
			"Yeah - cluster of heartbeats."
			He flexed his throat and unhinged his jaw, as did his packmate. They both let out an ethereal, alien song - one high-pitched enough that the bats in Wyrmrock went crazy.
			"Canines." he nodded. "A couple of them. A humanoid, too - must be the Commandant."
			"217 must be in there. She *has* to be. As for the other... they must be another sibling. More of my people."
			Connor gently stroked him between the ears.
			"This is the big moment. We get our revenge, and you get your sister back. After that... we hunt the rest of them down."
			"No time to dawdle, then." Sparky smiled. The two rose, and stretched their legs out.
			Connor closed his eyes, and focused. He flexed his thighs and calves, and felt his hot blood rush to them, saturating them with mutant power.
			Whatever the Commandant had done to him... it was going to be his undoing.
			The two rushed forward, and jumped. Their legs kicked into the roof's edge, smashing the metal downwards as they launched upwards. They landed on a skylight, crashing down.
			They landed on the ground, their arrival punctuated by raining shards of glass. 
			"COMMANDANT!" Connor roared. "SHOW YOURSELF!"
			His scream echoed in the cold, metal unit. He was answered by the sound of scraping, as a Super-Agent walked out from a storage crate, wielding twin machetes and clad in thick kevlar armour. 
			A television screen, which hanged from the wall, flashed to life. The Commandant's image flickered onto the screen.
			"Good evening, freaks." he grinned sadistically.
			"YOU FUCKING COWARD!" Connor howled. "SHOW YOUR FACE AND *DIE LIKE A MAN!*"
			"It's cute, honestly. You think you two little shits could kill me." he laughed. "And honestly, I think I may have tortured you a little too well. I tell you I'm somewhere, and mere minutes later you come running? You must miss me."
			"WHERE'S 217? WHERE'S MY SISTER?!" Sparky roared.
			"Oh, Six! Good to see you again." the Commandant smirked.
			At that, the Agent was joined by a pair of snarling, muscular mastiffs. It was barely visible past their fur, but the smell of their blood confirmed it - there was super-serum in their black veins.
			"She's not here, but don't worry - you have company. Project Fenrir wasn't a *complete* failure - that blood we harvested was given to these... mangy, rabid mutts."
			The twin Werewolves assumed a fighting stance.
			"You take the dogs - don't kill them." Connor whispered firmly, morphing blades from his wrists. "I'll fight the Agent."
			"Save some for me." Sparky snarled back, eyes burning red.
			"Sic 'em, boys!" The Commandant barked. "Agent Weiss - kill him."

			Connor wasn't here to fool around - he was here for blood. He spun forwards like a vengeful tornado, his blades ripping through the air. Weiss darted back, then knelt down and crossed his machetes, catching Connor's right.
			Under his mask, Connor grinned. His left blade burst forwards, aimed straight for Weiss's gut.
			Not fast enough. Weiss turned, twisting his blades so Connor's fell forward, and then he countered. Connor dodged the first machete, but the second nicked his neck.
			First blood. Connor felt the wound close up in moments, and snarled viciously.
			He roared, charging forwards again.

			At first, Sparky's wolven form intimidated the lesser canids. But then both remembered what the Commandant would do if they failed, and their black-veined eyes darkened with furor.
			"Listen to me! I don't want to hurt you!" he pleaded, as he slammed the backside of his paw around the head of one. He was careful not to catch it with his claws.
			The other used the opening to sink his teeth into Sparky's back leg, tearing hot blood and red meat.
			He howled in shock and pain, before turning and beating that one down. It got back up in short order.
			Sparky turned his head, and saw Connor's fight. His pupils shrank as they caught the Commandant's image.

			"DIE!" Connor demanded, as the tip of his blade sank into Weiss's thigh.
			Most men - hell, most Super-Agents - would've been thrown off by that. Weiss simply used his proximity to drive his own blade through Connor's hand.
			Connor screamed in rage as the blade shunted in between his carpal bones, popping out of his palm. Weiss pulled the blade backwards, splitting his hand in two.
			He flipped, and clutched his hand tight, setting the bones back and morphing a bandage to bind them. His eyes flashed crimson, and he formed bucklers over his wristblades.
			"Ah, finally - you've figured out you're not invincible, eh?" the Commandant taunted. "In fact, I'd say you're quite vincible."
			"Fuck you." Connor spat, his armour thickening and calcifying. He raced forwards, and the two monsters - one in form, one in soul - clashed again.

			Sparky snarled as another chunk of flesh tore out from his hide. He turned, and bit the scruff of the one who did it. He raised up on his hind legs, and threw it across the unit.
			Breathing space. He pounced on the other forcing it to its back.
			For normal canines, that would be it. The loser would submit, accepting that the winner would have its throat otherwise.
			The super-mastiff went right for Sparky's throat, instead. Sparky darted back just in time.
			"Please! Stop fighting me! I'm on your side! I want to stop the Commandant!" he begged.
			No answer. This wasn't one of his people - just an animal. A raging, monstrous animal.
			Sparky closed his scarlet eyes for a second.
			"I'm sorry." he whispered, as he ripped out its throat.
			He turned, as the other was sprinting towards him. He bowed his head in shame, and went for the kill.

			Connor snarled as Weiss's machete was knocked backwards by his buckler. He saw his opening and pounced forwards, paying him back in kind with a slash across the chest.
			Weiss's armour was shredded and torn, and his skin was raked and bloody - but he wasn't beaten. Not yet.
			He brought his blades together, holding them side-by-side. He half-closed his eyes, and breathed out slowly.
			Connor charged, pointing his own blades forward. He was going to impale this son of a bitch.
			Weiss held position. He felt his heart beat with anticipation. Then, he struck.
			Connor was tired. Exhausted, even. So exhausted, his reflexes were a nanosecond too late.
			Weiss's blades swept in a horizontal motion, clashing into Connor's forearms. The bucklers absorbed the damage, bending and cracking as his arms swung outwards.
			Connor went to close the opening, to put his guard back up, to do *something.*
			Too late.
			Weiss twisted his blades to their sides, and drove them through a gap in Connor's ribs.
			They sank through his armour, his lungs, and punched out through his back.
			Connor went to scream - instead, blood poured from his mouth and nose, as he gurgled in pain.
			Weiss gripped the hilts of his blades, and pushed Connor to his knees.
			"Hah..." the Commandant chuckled. "I expected more. Goodbye, Connor."
			Weiss placed his foot against Connor's sturnum, and pulled his blades free - slowly. Grinning.
			The blades glinted in the dim light, as he crossed them - holing them like shears ready to take the Werewolf's head.
			The blades tore through the air, sailing inward.
			Their impact sent a shock through the air, as they crashed into Connor's forearms.
			"No..." he gurgled. "NO!"
			Weiss struggled, but couldn't break past the Werewolf's determined guard.
			Connor was a lot of things. A lot more, lately.
			He was not someone who knew when to die.
			"GRAAAAGH!" Sparky howled, slamming into Weiss's side. He skidded to a halt as Weiss crashed into a wall.
			Connor spat a globule of blood, and forced himself to rise.
			Weiss planted his blades in the ground, using their support to get back up. He looked at the dead mastiffs, and laughed cruelly.
			"Oh dear, Six. It's not the first time you've seen your misbegotten kind die, is it? First time you've killed them, though." the Commandant chimed in.
			"You killed them. We just put them out of their misery." Sparky snarled grimly.
			"And if you wanna see 'killing,' then we're happy to oblige." Connor added. He readied his blades, as his lungs scabbed over.
			Weiss gripped the hilts tightly, as his eyes frantically darted side to side.
			The Werewolves charged in.
			Sparky hit first. Weiss's blade cut across his muzzle, but the crimson-eyed beast was unfazed. His teeth sank into Weiss's side, ripping out chunks of hot meat.
			Connor, meanwhile, sent his own blades down - ripping off Weiss's right hand. He screamed in pain, but then Sparky's claws sank into his throat.
			Connor grabbed the fallen machete, and swept as hard as he could.
			Weiss's body fell to the ground. His head landed a few feet away.
			"Credit where it's due." the Commandant grinned. "The data we've gained from this encounter is... invaluable."
			Sparky's hackles rose.
			Connor didn't move. His blades stayed forward, tense. "Agreed. We're going to make you feel everything you did to us. But first - where's 217?"
			The Commandant tilted his head, as if considering it. "Still on that, huh?"
			A faint crackle ran through the walls.
			Connor noticed it first. Not heard - felt. A low, irregular pulse under the metal floor. His eyes narrowed.
			"Well, now." the Commandant grinned. "Isn't this a nice trip down memory lane?"
			Connor's stare tightened. "What did you do?"
			"Not the first time Six has watched his kind die because of me. And definitely not the first time you've been buried."
			Connor went still. He tilted his head, but then, his irises shrank to pinpoints. His twin heartbeats turned to hums of terror.
			"Ah... The penny drops."
			Sparky's red gaze darted to his packmate. "Connor...?"
			"RUN!" he screamed.
			"What?! Why?!"
			"PLASTIC! IN THE WALLS!"
			Too late.
			The sound came first: a deep, mechanical *thump* from inside the walls.
			Then heat.
			The world around him erupted into flame. A massive explosion shook the building, and down it came.

			Sparky pulled himself out of the wreckage first. He frantically started digging, cutting his paw pads apart on the shrapnel. Finally, he unearthed Connor, who took a sharp intake of breath.
			The ringing in his ears was deafening. His vision blurred as he came to, the world around him a hazy mess of rubble and smoke. He groaned, disoriented, but alive.
			"Connor! Come on, we've got to go! The police will be here soon!"
			The sound of sirens wailing in the distance cut through the haze. Connor tried to rise, but looked back in horror. His hand was pinned under an entire wall's worth of rubble.
			His hearts raced as panic set in. He tugged at the debris, his breath coming in sharp gasps, but his hand remained firmly caught.
			"No... no, no, no..." he stuttered.
			He shifted his weight, tried to use his enhanced strength, but it was useless. His hand was trapped, and couldn't leave unless he freed it.
			Sparky put all his might into shifting the mess, but he could barely budge it.
			"Connor, I... I'm not strong enough." he cried.
			A grim realisation dawned on him.
			He morphed a blade from his costume. The knife's edge gleamed under the light. His free hand shook, trembling with urgency. He gritted his teeth and pressed the blade into his trapped forearm.
			Squelch.
			Shk.
			The world slowed. The pain was like nothing he'd ever felt before - sharp, intense, and relentless.
			It coursed through him, amplifying every sensation, turning his vision dark at the edges.
			Squelch again.
			Shk-shk.
			SNAP.
			With a final, brutal motion, he freed himself, his body recoiling from the sheer agony of it all. As he pulled free, the flesh ripped, and his wrist-joint popped. His bones were too strong to cut through - the amputation left his arm-bone sticking out from the stump, unblemished by the damage. He rose to his feet, breathless, bloodied, and battered.
			The world slowed down to a standstill. If normal pain could sharpen a mind - what could this pain do?
			He tensed, squeezing his eyes shut. Despite his eyelids being closed, his irises glowed with such a bright, brilliant red, that they shone past the skin. The glow faded, and the bleeding finally stopped. A bark from Sparky shook him from his stupor, and the pair sprinted up a wall back to their overlook, just as police and fire engines poured onto the site.

		The Loss of a Hand
		______________________________
		SCENE
			It had been a hundred years. It had been a couple of seconds.
			Connor woke up on the roof. As he did, Sparky rushed over, and licked his face frantically.
			"Are you okay?" he asked, worried.
			"Hah... I'm fine. Just blacked out for a moment." he nodded, his head feeling both light and heavy.
			He morphed back down into his civilian clothes, and reached into his pocket. He pulled out a small pack of cigarettes.
			"Thank god these weren't squished back there." he chuckled, holding one in his mouth, and lighting it. The motion was tricky with one hand, but he managed.
			"Why do you burn those stinky sticks?" Sparky asked.
			"Honestly? Not much use to me these days. Downside of being a super-powered mutant is you can't get anything out of nicotine." he shrugged. "Still, the ritual of it... calms me down, I guess."
			Sparky nodded, and sat down with his packmate. "What happens now?" he asked.
			"Now? Now we see if I can grow back limbs." Connor laughed and coughed. "If I can't... we may need to rethink our operation."
			He leant back. "I've been putting off asking you... maybe because I'm scared about what you'll say. But... this whole thing with the Commandant..."
			"He was... he was right." Sparky said, nearly gagging on the words. "We thought we were better, but all it took was one phone call, and it's like we're back in the cages again."
			Connor looked away for a minute, before turning back.
			"My memories of it all... they're jumbled. I can't remember us escaping the first time. But... you remember, don't you?"
			Sparky thought for a moment.
			"All my life, I remember being in this cage. Being hurt by the bad men." he began. "And none of them ever cared. They just kept hurting me. Sometimes it was for fun, sometimes I think they were being curious, but it was always cruel. And..." he paused. "And then, one day, the bad men brought you in. You were hurt, badly - but alive. They chained you up. I wasn't in the room, but I could hear you screaming as they hurt you too."
			Connor leant forward, listening intently.
			"I kept hearing them talking about programming. I think they wanted to train you. They kept saying these specific words - 'Listen and Obey.'"
			Connor flinched at the words. Even hearing them telepathically from a wolf didn't soften their blow.
			"Every time they did, they hurt you." Sparky continued. "One day, your screaming was louder than ever before. I heard you thrashing and smashing about, and you burst out of the door they held you in. You came running out, and I knew you were different. You looked at me, and I didn't see cruelty, just sadness. I begged you to let me out, and you heard me, and you saved me."
			Connor rubbed his temples with his intact hand, processing. "So... We broke out, together?"
			"Yes. We ran for miles and miles." Sparky nodded. "But they caught up to us. They overwhelmed us, and dragged us away. They separated us - I never knew what happened to you afterwards."
			Connor looked downwards. "And... they brought you back to the place I found you?"
			"No. They brought me back to where we first met." Sparky explained. "But they were worried you might come back for me. So they moved me to the other place - the one where you and Ivan saved me."
			Connor leaned back. "Did, um... did you ever see me leave on my own? The Commandant... he pulled a trick on me."
			"No, never." Sparky shook his head.
			Connor stroked his chin. "Makes sense. We escape together, then after they bring us both back, the Commandant stages another escape to crush my hopes of leaving. They must've somehow wiped my memories of us getting out, too."
			Sparky looked away. "They were cruel. After meeting so many normal humans, I don't get it. Humans aren't so different to wolves. You're naturally decent. So what's wrong with them?"
			Connor sighed. "I don't know, bud. They're cruel. Evil. Monsters..."
			Sparky thought for a moment. "The word he used - Fenrir. That's what they called me, too."
			"Project Fenrir... That explains the super-dogs earlier." Connor nodded, visibly joining the dots. "Whatever made me and the Super-Agents, Fenrir made you and the dogs."
			"They're building an army." Sparky realised in horror.
			"Still... it doesn't explain why we're different. I mean, you couldn't hear the dogs talking, could you?"
			"No, nothing." Sparky shook his head. "This weird connection we have... I think it's just us."

			Connor paused. He closed his eyes, hesitated, and reached out. He placed his hand on Sparky's head, and their minds touched.
			Fear. Pain. Rage. All swirling through his mind, like he was pulling the depths of the ocean to the surface. He reached inwards, and Sparky let him in.
			This 'mind-bond' they had was utterly alien to both. The flashes, the shared dreams... and now this. Connor stretched his mind's eye into Sparky's subconsciousness, and watched. He saw himself, bursting out of a steel door, drenched in blood and howling in pain. He felt Sparky's memories, his emotions, his senses... the link grew stronger. Sparky saw through Connor's eyes, and Connor through Sparky's. The line where one ended and the other began had blurred into oblivion.
			Connor saw the torment Sparky had faced. Horrific surgeries. Agonising tests. He watched as the rest of Sparky's litter died, until only he was left.
			Sparky saw Connor's own pain. The torments. And others, too. He saw the moment Vince was arrested. He saw the days in the Bogside where Connor's grandfather beat him. He saw a blazing inferno in a car, with his grandmother's burning corpse hanging out. And deeper still, he watched through Connor's eyes as drove a knife through an older man's head.
			It was too much. The two pulled back, and rubbed their skulls, regaining their senses of self. After a short while, they both opened their eyes, and looked down - as though visibly checking which one they were.
			"You okay?" Connor asked.
			"Yeah, I... I'm Sparky, right?" he replied.
			"Yeah. Which means I'm Connor... Alright, I'm okay now. What... What the hell was that?"
			"I don't know." Sparky shrugged. "It felt like we became one person for a moment."
			Connor nodded, and closed his eyes again.
			"Who was that man?" Sparky asked.
			"Which one?"
			"The one you stabbed. I felt that memory..." Sparky explained.
			Connor sighed. "James Laverty." he finally said, half-spitting the name. "He... he was mine and Amy's foster-carer."
			"What's a foster-carer?" Sparky tilted his head.
			"They're supposed to be caregivers." Connor explained. "A bit like what I am to you. Someone who isn't your parent, but raises you anyway. But he... he was a monster."
			Worse, deeper memories washed into Connor's mind. Flashes of Laverty... and what he did to Amy. He reached his hand back out, and rejoined his mind with Sparky.
			Sparky took in the flashes, then pulled his head back in disgust.
			"Good work." he nodded. "But you were a pup back then?"
			"Yeah, it was before I got my powers." Connor shrugged. "I don't know how, I just... I went berserk. After that, I was taken away by the police. Thankfully, they decided not to press charges, and that's how me and Amy came to live with Vince."
			Connor sighed. He recalled the memories he'd gleaned from Sparky.
			"I saw your memories too, you know. You... You survived all of that."
			Sparky jumped up, and rested his head on Connor's lap. "You did too. Until I met you, I never knew humans could be nice."
			"You've always been so good with people though." Connor replied. "When Amy came back on your first night with us, you were so good with her. And you were just as good with our other friends."
			"I guess... It's because I had you." Sparky mused. "You saved me from that place. So, I trust you. And that means, I trust who you trust."
			Connor smiled warmly. "I trust you too."
			He went to stroke Sparky's head, before realising he was using the wrong arm. He chuckled grimly.
			"We've both been through hell." he began. "And that's not gonna heal any time soon. But we have each other. Before I had you, I was... I was a wreck. I wanted to die, because the pain was too much. But then you came along. And you were the only creature on Earth who could know what I was going through. More than that, you needed me as much as I needed you. So looking after you... helps me."
			"What do you mean?" Sparky tilted his head.
			"I mean, when it was just me, I could let myself fall apart. But with you here, I have to stick around to help you. Not only that, when you're suffering, I've gotta do something. I can justify not helping myself - I can't justify not helping you. And through that, I learned to help myself. Throgh being kind to you, I learned to be kind to myself. Through helping absolve you, I... I found my own absolution."
			Sparky nuzzled his face into Connor's chest.
			"You're right. We're the only things like us. Which means we can get through this pain... together."

			At the same time, Naismith was overlooking the smouldering ruins. Nina approached him.
			"Good news, sir. We were able to shift the wreckage. We've recovered the hand." she said.
			"In what condition?" Naismith asked.
			"Pristine, sir." she replied. "I've already called the FIs to prep for immediate analysis. Though it's missing a lot of bone, they should still be able to extract prints and DNA."
			"Missing bone?" Naismith tilted his head.
			Nina nodded. "I'm no FI, but it looked to me as though he'd cut the flesh around the bone, and then just pulled until the wrist popped off. As a result, there's the flesh from the wrist, but no forearm-bone. Well, either that, or he doesn't have forearm bones." she chuckled.
			Naismith smirked. "The man's a bloody alien, I'll tell ya."
			As he said this, the hand was brought past them in a container. Nina yelped, as did an FI - the hand was *twitching.*
			"Jesus..." Naismith muttered. "What the fuck?"
			"The techs will have a field day, sir." Nina nodded, shuddering.
			"Well then." Naismith smiled. "Let's get to work."

		Trauma-dumping
		______________________________
		SCENE
			It was past midnight now. Connor had been dreading this, but it needed to be done.
			He opened his flat's door.
			Immediately, his eyes flashed red for a second. He saw Amy's heartbeat behind her door.
			She was sat against it, as if barricading herself away.
			Timidly, he approached. He could hear her breathing quicken as he walked, and her heart skip a beat as he knocked.
			"Amy..." he whispered. "It's... it's me. Connor."
			She didn't say anything. She just silently sobbed, covering her mouth so as not to scream.
			He sat down against her door. Even without super-senses, she could feel her brother's presence opposite her.
			Connor sighed. "These... these men, they shot me in the head. They took me away, and they... did something to me. Experimented on me. Tortured me. Made me into... this."
			Her breathing trembled.
			"I wanted to tell you..." he continued, his voice cracking. "I... I was just scared. Scared it might put a target on your back, scared you'd think I was crazy, scared I *was* crazy... and scared that I'd scare you. Like now."
			She sniffled softly, clutching her knees.
			"I know it's a lot... I can't imagine how you are right now, but I..." he began, tears rolling down his face. "I could really use my sister right now."
			She took a deep breath, stood, and opened the door. He rose too.
			She wordlessly pulled him in for an embrace. He held his arms out awkwardly, before wrapping her in them. They both took a moment to breathe.

			Finally, she pulled back, and looked at him, before going pale again.
			"Uh... What the hell?! What happened? W-where the fuck is your hand?!" she stammered, horrified.
			"Oh, shit." Connor sighed, sitting her down.
			"What happened?!" she repeated. Sparky jumped up, and curled into a ball next to her. She absently stroked his fur, grounding herself.
			"I got pinned under some rubble." Connor explained nonchalantly.
			"You... You cut off your own hand?" she asked.
			"...yes." he nodded. "It was either that, or get caught by the police."
			"Can you grow hands back? Is that one of your superpowers?"
			Connor allowed himself a chuckle. "Superpowers?"
			"You *do* know I saw you outside the Horse, right? Getting shot in the chest six times and barely flinching?" she cocked an eyebrow.
			"Fair enough." he grinned. "Anyway, I'm not sure. Never lost a limb before. But..." he began, pulling up his sleeve. "It's healed a little. Look at the bone - there was more sticking out ealier. Hell, my wrist-bone seems to be growing back too."
			He pointed at the stump, revealing a fledgling wrist-joint forming above his arm-bone. His skin and flesh was creeping up the bone, covering it neatly. He hadn't looked at it in the light, but now he could see - His bone was dark, as though someone mixed calcium with coal. His brain flashed back to his school chemistry lessons, but he shook his head.
			"Plus, I've grown back teeth before, and I've healed away scars." he shrugged.
			Amy gulped, and held his stump gently.
			"So... you're gonna be okay?" she asked finally.
			"Probably. If not, I'm sure I can get some decent prosthetics from the KGB." he answered nonchalantly.
			"The KGB?" she cocked her eyebrow.
			"Long story. But yeah, the KGB are helping me. Whoever these freaks I'm fighting are, they're clearly connected to fascists - and for all their faults, the KGB *hate* fascism."
			Amy nodded slightly, then allowed herself a chuckle. "Christ, if Vince knew you were working with communists, he'd be jumping for joy."
			Connor laughed. "Just wait 'til we get the IRA on-side."
			She giggled, then went quiet. "So... You're the 'Werewolf' people have been talking about?"
			"I have *no* idea where that nickname comes from." Connor chuckled grimly. Amy allowed herself a laugh.
			"Yeah. It's fucking lame." she snarked, still in shock.

			She paused, hesitant. "You... you mentioned torture?"
			Connor sighed, and nodded. "The Commandant - the guy who phoned earlier. He put me through hell."
			"Why? Why would he do that?"
			"Not sure yet. But either way, he kidnapped me, tortured me, and changed me."
			He took a deep breath, before continuing.
			"It wasn't just physical. I mean, they cut me up, zapped me, put me in an ice bath, waterboarded me, you name it. But the worst was the tricks."
			"Tricks?"
			"One time, he let me think I was escaping. Just as I was about to leave, he shot me, and brought me back in. Not only that, they fucked with my head somehow... the memories are jumbled."
			"So how did you escape? How did you come back home?"

		Pre-Whiplash

			He sent a haymaker aiming right for her head. As it sailed through the air, her eyes flashed violet, and he felt it move - as if some hidden force was pushing it away. All the momentum was lost, as it went right by the side of her head. Meanwhile, she pulled two knives from her belt, and sank them repeatedly into his torso.

			To his horror, he watched as her eyes shifted, and they suddenly veered off course, flying past her with not a single scratch.
			"How the fuck..." he muttered, before realising.

He grabbed her by the head as hard as he could, and rather than stabbing, he pushed his free hand into her arm. Despite his lack of momentum, it broke past the skin and into the flesh beneath.

			Finally, a haymaker from her sent him spinning to the ground. Landing on his back, she planted her boot on his neck. He gripped her heel, trying desperately to move it, but felt even the tiny gasps of air he could breathe be pulled from his lungs.

			"Thanks..." he nodded, clearing his throat. He turned to face her. "I'd say don't do anything strenuous, but..."
			She reached down, and felt her ribcage mechanically. The ribs were still fractured, but her lung wasn't leaking air anymore. Her heel - the one Connor snapped - was bound in a cast.
			"I managed to vent your lung when you came in. Normally I'd say we put a tube in, but air build-up is minimal. If your breathing gets worse again, come right back in."
			"Thanks, doc." Connor nodded. He motioned, and Whiplash rose. She strained, but got to her feet. She limped as the pair left the back-alley clinic.

			"Why'd you save me?" she asked.
			Connor paused, folding his arms.
			"Three reasons. First, because I wanna know some things. Second... well, you're not with Paladin, so there's no inherent reason to kill you. Third... You were in a lot of pain. And I could help."
			"Oh, don't tell me you've fallen for me." she grinned.
			"I do that." he sighed. "Masking. I do it all the time. I quip during fights, I banter with my friends, I--"
			"Spare me the psychoanalysis." she cut in harshly. "What's the real reason?"
			"I've just given three."
			"Three bullshit reasons." she scoffed. "You wouldn't save me unless there was something in it for you. Something more than a little chat."
			"Is it that hard to believe I would help you?" he tilted his head.
			"Yes." she nodded curtly. "I tried to kill you."
			Connor sighed again. "You know, one guy shot at me with a sniper rifle. Then he unloaded a shotgun into my chest. He's now one of my closest allies."
			"'Allies?' Are you asking me on a date?" she snarked.
			"I'm guessing the guys who paid you won't be too happy." he shrugged. "And I'm guessing someone with your... 'talents...' would be a lot of trouble for them to go after. Why not work together?"
			She looked away. "No. It's too dangerous."
			"Whiplash." he said firmly. "I can see in slow motion, so I saw what you can do."
			She sighed, leaning back. "It's called Trajectory Manipulation. A form of telekinesis."
			"How do you do it?"
			"How do you shit knives and darts out of your hands?" she chuckled. "I... I was only a little girl when they took me."
			Connor nodded, wordlessly encouraging her. She hesitated, and folded her arms - as if putting up a shield.
			"They put you in this airtight pod, filled with lukewarm water, and they whack an oxygen mask on your face." she continued. Her eyes squeezed shut, as if she was back in the pod once again. "You can't hear, smell, taste, feel, see... complete sensory deprivation."
			"How long do you stay in?" he asked.
			"As long as it takes." she shuddered. "They let you out once you manage to tell them the password. And the only way to get the password... is to read someone's mind."
			"How do you do that?"
			"That's what the deprivation is for." she nodded. "If your five senses are shut off, you're forced to rely on your sixth. That's why they lock up kids - apparently, children's neurons are less insulated, which makes them more receptive to... to that kind of training."
			"And once your sixth sense is activated... you're what, a psychic?"
			"Esper. That was the term they used." she shrugged. "You still need to be trained, though. Most of our 'powers' are far too complicated to use right off the bat. For example, I can manipulate trajectories, but I never trained in general telekinesis. For my... line of work... you need a more subtle touch."
			Connor cleared his throat. "So, this... psychic laboratory, or whatever - who are they?"
			"ODIN." she shrugged. "Operational Directorate for Investigative Neurokinetics. They were originally a CIA black project called MKULTRA; when they realised they were *actually* on to something, they went solo."
			"ODIN... they really squeezed to make that acronym fit, eh?" he snarked.
			She let out a soft laugh. "You're telling me. What with us, PaladinCorp, and Eidolon - you have a habit of getting people with ominous names to try and kill you."
			"You said you weren't with Paladin. So, ODIN - the're the ones who want me dead?"
			"No. They produce assassins. The man who *hired* me wants you dead." she chuckled grimly. "And now... he'll be after me, and so will they..."
			"Why would they come after you?"
			"Because I failed." she admitted, choking up a little - not out of shame, but fear. "I know the punishment for failing and not dying."
			"Then stay here." he said softly. "If they come here, we can fight them off together."
			She looked at him, her eyes trembling slighty. "I... I can't. I've got to go off the grid - at least for a while."
			"I get it." Connor nodded gently. "But listen - if you do need help, come to the Singing Horse - it's a nightclub in Redbridge. Ask for me - the owner knows me."
			"Why are you doing this?" she asked, her brow furrowing.
			"Doing what? Being kind?"
			"Yes! Why would you do that?!" she hissed.
			"Because... I know what it's like to be tortured." he shrugged. "And to be hunted. And it's my fault you're in this situation. And... well, I'm something of a superhero. It's my *job* to be kind."
			She paused, looking at him up and down. The monster in the kevlar suit - her target, her prey... it didn't make sense.
			She hesitantly reached out her hand. He paused, but took it, and their consciousnesses shot against each other.
			She saw the Commandant's torment of him. His body twisting and reshaping against his will. He saw... nothing. The horror of nothingness. The pod.
			It was too much. They pulled away, and rubbed their temples in unison.
			She turned away, then turned her head back. She pulled off her domino mask, and gulped.
			"Before they took me..." she began, choking on her words. "My name was Olivia. Olivia Cunningham."
			Connor hesitated, but his mask rippled and melted away.
			"I'm Connor. Connor Barrett."
			Whiplash - Olivia - bowed her head, and walked away into the night.
			Connor stood there, as she faded into the fog. The kevlar melted back down into his soft red hoodie, and he pulled the cloth closer for warmth. He took a deep breath, and smiled sadly.

The force of the impact was enough to make the warehouse floor tremble. The Giant's skull caved in with a sickening crunch, and blood splattered across the cold concrete.

			"Well, not to make light of it, but they're not normally this big." the man chuckled. Above the mask, Chloe's eyes creased - she was smirking. Satisfied he'd relaxed her a little, the man pulled out a circular saw.
			"So, I'll use this to open up his chest cavity, and then we'll use the spreader to open up the ribcage. From there, we can begin extracting his internal organs, and take a look at them."
			"Mm-hm." Chloe responded, trembling at the thought.
			The man smiled, and began to use the saw. Despite the size and high quality, the saw took much, much longer than usual to cut through.
			"Hmph... Get... In... There!" the man said, finally cutting in. "Whew, okay, so, initial findings?" he looked up at Chloe.
			"Well..." Chloe said, clicking her pen to begin writing on her notepad, "His skin and muscles are clearly much tougher than normal humans. The fact that the saw is struggling to cut through his chest means his tissue density is far beyond normal levels. It's like trying to slice through a reinforced steel plate with a butter knife. The muscle fibres are denser, almost like they've been artificially toughened."
			"Very good." the man nodded. "External injuries?"
			"You mean aside from the mulch pile where his head should be?" Chloe asked, making the man chuckle. "I can see a bullet wound... there." she pointed to a hole in the chest. "According to officer statements, this was caused by a high-caliber bullet fired by a sniper rifle. Police ballistic analysis reported that the bullet had a carbon plating on the tip, which made it much sharper - so the assailants knew that this man needed a lot to take down."
			"Any other, non-fatal injuries?" the man asked, waiting to see Chloe's reaction.
			"Hmm... there!" she said, pointing to his leg and abdomen. "Small wounds, likely caused by the officer's attempts to shoot him. The bullets made an impact, causing friction burns and bruising, but did not pierce the skin. And... teeth marks on the shoulder, consistent with the description of the 'Werewolves' present. But what stands out to me is the depth of those marks. They're not just punctures; they're almost like the bite force was so extreme that it crushed through the muscle fibres and into the bone. How could something bite harder than our saws? Anyway..." she banished the thought.
			"Very good!" the man said, satisfied. "Okay, let's open him up. Spreader?"
			Chloe handed him the tool, and the man began to spread the ribcage open. He strained under the pressure of using the tool, not expecting it to be so difficult. Eventually, the giant's chest opened with a sickening crunch.
			"Right, now, before I start cutting about willy-nilly, any thoughts about his chest cavity?" the man asked. Chloe leant over to look inside, and gasped audibly.
			"That's... two hearts? Three lungs? And... Four kidneys?! No... those two aren't kidneys. They're adrenal glands, swollen beyond belief." she said, shocked.
			"Wait, adrenal glands? Hang on... You're right." the man tilted his head. "Whatever this thing is, it's had a lot of work done."
			Chloe shuddered, writing down this news. The man began extracting the giant's organs, one-by-one, and placing them in jars for later study. He also cut open the giant's leg, and took a sample of muscle tissue and bone marrow. Once finished, he closed the man back up, and breathed a sigh of relief.
			"Final thoughts?" he asked.
			"You'd think the extra organs would be the biggest one..." Chloe said unsurely. "But I think those adrenal glands could be just as important. The only reason they'd be that big on purpose would be if they're creating more than just adrenaline."
			She thought deeply.
			The man smiled, impressed. "Bet you didn't think your uni placement would be like this, eh?"
			Chloe chuckled. "I'm just glad the Christmas holidays are coming up."
			The man laughed. "Okay, we're all done. Let's get him sealed back up, and you have the joy of dissecting those glands."
			"Yay." Chloe cheered sarcastically, and they hauled the Giant into the freezer. Even with lifting aids and several organs removed, he was incredibly heavy.
			The two breathed out in relief, and left the autopsy room.
