			Both boys were clearly stronger than they looked. The other boys tried to split them up, but were tossed aside by the two berserker teens.
			Finally, a group of teachers came running over. With considerable effort, both were dragged away from each other.

			Half an hour had passed, and both boys sat in the detention room in school. The teacher meant to be supervising them had simply left and locked the door. Both boys, now bruised, sat on opposite ends of the classroom. Both maintained permanent scowls on their faces, and kept their arms folded.
			This silence carried on for a good while - longer than most 15-year-olds could've managed. Finally, Connor took a deep breath.
			"This is all your fault." he growled.
			"Me?!" Trey snapped. "You're the one who went all psycho at me!"
			"You're the one who ruined my homework!"
			"Well, you're a weirdo!"
			"Fuck you!"
			Both boys were standing, ready to go for another round. Connor took a deep breath, and sat back down.
			"I'm sorry." he said through gritted teeth. "Actually, no, I'm not. Today's a really shitty day, and you made it 10 times worse."
			"Oh, boo hoo. The weirdo had a rough day." Trey mocked.
			"Shut up!" Connor snarled. "It's Bloody Sunday, if you've gotta know. The tenth one, as well."
			"It's bloody Friday, you idiot." Trey scoffed.
			"I mean the one in 2001! Oh, whatever. Not like you'd get it, anyway." Connor rolled his eyes.
			"What's that supposed to mean?!" Trey slammed his hands on the desk. "You think I'm stupid or something?!"
			"Yeah." Connor grinned.
			Trey went to be enraged, but instead, he simply chuckled.
			"Ugh... look. I'm sorry I ruined your coursework. And I'm sorry I ruined your stupid holiday."
			"It's not a holiday." Connor said curtly. "Ugh, I'm fuckin' sick of this shite. I'm sick of living next to you people!"
			"The fuck do you mean?" Trey snapped back, offended. "Oh, what, you're a racist now?"
			"Fuck off! I mean the English! None of yous even acknowledge what happened! What yous took from me! *WHO* yous took from me!"
			Connor's anguished scream echoed in the room. It went deathly silent, and Connor tried - and failed - to regain his composure.
			Trey covertly searched "Bloody Sunday 2001" on his smartphone while Connor rocked back and forth. He saw a brief article detailing it - the opening shots of the Bogside War.
			He walked over, tentatively.
			"Hey, I... I'm sorry that happened to you guys. I didn't know any of that - it's not like they teach it here."
			Connor looked over, his eyes bloodshot from silent tears.
			"I don't mean *you.*" Connor finally admitted. "I just mean... I'm tired of it. I don't fit in here, everyone calls me a weirdo, I'm just... I'm done."
			"Hey..." Trey sighed. "I'm sorry for calling you a weirdo. I was just going along with the guys, that's all."
			"Why?" Connor asked.
			Trey tried for a good while to think of a decent excuse. He couldn't, so he just sighed again.
			"I shouldn't've. I guess... if we're picking on you, then they're not picking on me. And yeah, I know, that doesn't make it okay. Look, I know what it's like to be judged by other people, if it helps." he began.
			"How?"
			"I'm black, you weir---sorry. I meant 'idiot.'"

			"I'm sorry, too. I overreacted. My uncle always says I've got a bad temper."
			"Eh, I gave as good as I got. You're lucky those teachers split us up."
			"Yeah, right. If they hadn't come, I'd've thrashed you."
			"Sure thing. Keep telling yourself that."
			The boys tried to maintain this rough charade, but both cracked, and began to laugh. Once the laughter died down, Trey spoke again.
			"You said 'who' we took from you. What did you mean?"

			"He can lift cars above his head - I think he'll be fine."

			"H-hi!" she waved awkwardly. "Uh... nice mask!"

			Connor tilted his head. "I... I appreciate that, but it's fine. This is Syndicate business."
			"That's okay!" she cut in. "I've been helping out, around here."

			"Uh--yeah, sure, no problem." she stammered, rising and leaving.
			"What's the problem?" Tommy asked.
			"The 'problem' is that I didn't send her to you to get involved in... our world." Connor sighed.
			"I know." Tommy nodded. "Believe it or not, she came to me. She said she was inspired by you, and wanted to do some good. And, well, my *other* computer nerd is a bit busy nowadays running around in a kevlar bodysuit."
			Connor looked away. "This is dangerous, Tommy. I mean, the Patriots are one thing, but Paladin? The Optimates?"
			"She's well aware of the risks, Connor. It's her choice."
			He hesitated, but released his shoulders, and headed back outside.
			Shannon was sat at a desk, browsing through the now-unencrypted files.
			"Oh, hi." she said nervously. "Is everything okay?"
			He smiled softly. "Yeah, it's fine. Just... this is really dangerous, you know? Working with us--with *me...* it puts a target on your back."
			"I'm already a target in this city." she countered. "I wouldn't've been kicked out and getting mugged if I wasn't... well, me. And *you* saved me, remember? And if I can do just a little something to make your job easier, to take just a little bit of weight off your shoulders - then that means I'm helping you save other people just like me."
			Connor sighed, but his eyes betrayed his pride. "When we last met, you said you were studying computing - not that you were a hacker."
			"Well..." she sheepishly admitted, "I've always been a tinkerer. And when I started at the workshop, I found a bunch of tools left by Connor - uh, the last techie - so I got a bit curious, started studying them, and now... well, it turns out I have a knack for it."
			Connor smiled. "You're sure you wanna do this?"
			"I'm sure. You can help people by beating up bad guys and saving the day. I can help by doing *this.*"
			He thought about it for a moment, and then nodded.
			"Well then... Welcome to the team, Shannon."
			"Glad to be here." she smiled warmly. "By the way, do I get a cool codename too?"
			"Maybe later." he grinned.

		Morgan Family Christmas
		______________________________
		SCENE
			The aftermath of Christmas dinner at the Jefferson household was peaceful, if a little sluggish. The room practically oozed warmth - the scent of cinnamon and roast goose still clung to the air. Bea lay sprawled across a reclining sofa, her stomach full, her eyelids heavy. Her year-younger sister, Tea, was fast asleep across the room, wrapped in a throw blanket. Their dad had retired upstairs for a nap, and their mum had disappeared into the bath nearly an hour ago, likely dozing there too.

However, where Bea's skin was a constellation of vitiligo, Tea's was a solid sheet of light-brown. Where Bea's eyes contrasted through heterochromia, Tea's were both a shimmering hazel.
			In most dynamics, the 'normal' sister would be the suave, confident one; while the 'abnormal' would be shy and socially deprived. The key word there was 'most.'
			Tea's clothes were almost impressively plain. A grey hoodie over light blue jeans - in this case, unbuttoned at the top to accommodate Christmas dinner. Her hair was as curly as Bea's, but rather than the bright and loud red-dyed afro bob that Bea had opted for, her thick curls had been bunched into a low ponytail, with a few strands dangling in front of her face. All in all, neither sister could be put into a label - fittingly, neither would desire to be.
			"Just a walk." Bea whispered. "I'll be back soon."
			The streets were cold and slick. The sky was darkening, the stars blurry behind thin clouds. Bea pulled her coat tighter as she reached the park. 
			Charlie stood waiting, hands in his coat pockets, eyes on the ground.
			He looked up and smiled as she approached. "Hey."
			"Hey!" she replied, breath puffing in the cold.
			"I didn't think you'd come." he began. His voice was low. "I thought maybe you'd changed your mind."
			"No, I just didn't want to stay long. Everyone's still up, mostly."
			He pulled a small wrapped box from his coat and handed it to her.
			Bea opened it carefully. Inside was a delicate silver bracelet.

			He smiled.
			She looked down at the bracelet again. "Thank you. Really."
			He reached forward, brushing her hair behind her ear. "You don't have to say anything. Just being here... it means more than you know."
			She nodded, pushing her face into his hand.
			"I wanted to give you something that reminded you how different you are. How real." he said. "Not like... the people around you."
			She shifted. "Charlie..."
			"I mean, it's nice they're there," he said, too quickly. "But they don't see you. Not like I do. You said yourself you feel like the extra in your own friend group sometimes."
			"I didn't mean it like that," she said, suddenly uncomfortable.
			He studied her for a moment, then reached for her hands. "Come back to mine?"
			She blinked. "What?"
			"Just for a bit." he said quickly. "I've got this bottle of wine I've been saving, and I made mince pies. I thought... maybe we could just have a moment. Something that's ours."
			"I can't, sorry. I should probably head back soon," she said, almost apologetically.
			His expression shifted. The smile disappeared. "Right."
			She frowned. "I'm sorry, I just - "
			"It's fine," he said sharply, pulling his hands away. "It's totally fine. I just thought maybe you'd want to spend time with me. Guess I misread things."
			"Charlie, I--"
			"No, it's okay. Seriously. Don't worry about it." His tone was brittle. "Enjoy your perfect little family night."
			"That's not fair," Bea said, a tremble in her voice.
			He turned away, jaw tight. "You know what? Just forget I asked. I shouldn't have. This was stupid."
			There was a beat of silence, and then, as suddenly as he had snapped, he softened.
			"I'm sorry," he said, running a hand through his hair. "God, I'm such an idiot. You didn't deserve that. I just... I missed you so much today. I guess I let it get to me."
			Bea stood frozen.
			"I'm sorry, Bea. I just thought... I thought we had something. And I thought maybe today, of all days, I'd matter enough to you to get a little of your time. But it's okay. Really."
			He offered a weak smile, eyes sad. "Go home. They'll miss you."
			Bea gulped, a lump in her throat. "Of course you matter to me. It's just... it's Christmas, you know? We see each other every day at uni."
			"You don't have to explain." he said, backing away.
			She didn't reply. She couldn't. Her feet felt stuck to the pavement.
			"Merry Christmas, Bea." he whispered.
			And then he was gone, his footsteps echoing off the wet stones, leaving her standing alone with the bracelet still in her hands.
			She sighed deeply.

What if Jack grows up hating me for breaking up his family? I... I'm sorry Nina. But I can't." she cried, and hung up the phone.

Max whimpered, but Naismith uncocked it, took out the magazine, and emptied the chamber. The ease at which he did this even when drunk was indicative of his skill at arms.

These occur due to an overstimulation of the sympathetic nervous system, which causes vasodilation in the brain, increasing pressure and causing the blood vessels to rupture."
			Morland raised an eyebrow but said nothing, so Chloe continued, tapping the screen to show the next slide.
			"At moderate doses, we start seeing seizures. The neurons in the brain become hyper-excitable due to an imbalance in the sodium and potassium ion channels. It's like a short circuit in the nervous system. The more the subject's body is exposed to Paradrenaline, the more severe the disruption becomes."
			Morland winced, his lips curling into a slight smile. "And at high doses?"
			Chloe's voice lowered, growing more serious. "At high doses, the symptoms are catastrophic. Strokes, aneurysms, and cerebral haemorrhages. The vasculature in the brain becomes too fragile, and the heart rate increases to dangerous levels, putting immense strain on the circulatory system."
			Morland watched her intently, considering her words. "But the superhumans, they survive these doses?"
			"Yes." she nodded. "We believe it's due to their enhanced anatomy. Their bodies seem to compensate for the damage. Their regenerative abilities kick in faster than normal, allowing them to recover from the worst effects. But it's still a temporary fix - they can only withstand so much before the damage becomes incapacitating."
			"The potential here..." he murmured. "If only we could mitigate these side effects."
			"I agree, sir." Chloe smiled. "First responders, firefighters, ambulance staff... they could all really benefit from something like this."
			Morland chuckled. "Yes, them too. But I think you'll find defence contractors pay more."
			Chloe gulped, disgusted. "Sir... you want to weaponise this?"
			Morland's expression turned grim. "Not a word of this leaves this room. Understood?"
			"But sir, we're supposed to report this to the police--"
			"Not a word." Morland interrupted. Chloe nodded.
			"Of course, sir." she said, looking down.
			"Any other discoveries?" he asked.
			"Oh, yes, there was one." she began, showing another slide. "This hormone - we've yet to identify a suitable natural analogue, so we're calling it XJK5 for the time being. It originates on xeno-chromosome 12 - as you know, sir, the Werewolf has an extra 15. Anyway, it seems to be correlated to, or downstream from, the paradrenaline - that is, rushes of paradrenaline trigger a release of XJK5, too. When applied to lab rats, it doesn't trigger the same side effects paradrenaline did - instead, it seems to change their thought processes. It amplifies their memory recall - they proved able to solve puzzles they'd done previously in much faster times - but reduces their creativity - new puzzles kept them stumped for much longer than normal."
			"Fascinating. Send me the results." Morland nodded, before leaving the room, and heading to his office.
			Chloe stood, and sighed.

			Morland pulled out his phone, and called a number - the Commandant.

			"Who's 'we', Morland?" the Commandant asked.

			"Yes. A substance she calls 'XJK5.' It sounds like its effects are similar to the truth serums we had before Zhao trashed everything..."
			"Good. Each finding brings us closer to rebuilding what he stole."

			"Don't get your knickers in a twist, Morland." the Commandant snapped.

	A Pack of Heroes

		FLASHBACK
			Grozny, Chechen ASSR. 18th of February, 2009.
			Separatist forces led by Islamist warlord Vadim Zamaldayev had captured the city. Recognising their position was untenable, Soviet Loyalists had organised a convoy to escape into Russia proper. But Zamaldayev's forces had spotted them, and mobbed nearby.
			The evacuation would have been doomed - were it not for the 9th Motor Rifle Division's timely arrival.
			This was going to be the Battle of Grozny.

			The Division's commander, Major Iosef Tarkovsky - an older man, with a nervous disposition - was surveying some maps, alongside his aides.
			"[It's a mess out there.]" Tarkovsky noted dryly.
			"[Yes, sir.]" an aide nodded. "[Our current strategy is to have Makharadze and Lebedev reinfoce Ahmadov - the de-facto leader of the Loyalist forces. From there, general Trepov will come in from the north, and close in on the insurgents. Once they are put to rout, we will complete the evacuation.]"
			"[Is there any hope of us taking the city?]" Tarkovsky asked wearily.
			"[I'm afraid not, sir. Even if Zamaldayev died here, the city is effectively lost to us. Our only hope is to cross back over the mountains, and pray Moscow hasn't fallen when we get there.]"
			"[So be it.]" Tarkovsky sighed. "[Begin the operation.]"

			An hour had passed. In Lebedev's brigade, the fighting was intense. Separatist forces anticipated the maneuver, and intercepted before Lebedev could reach the convoy.
			In the 3rd Company, Svetlana Popova was staff nurse. She hurriedly tried to stop the bleeding of a young, pimply Lance Corporal. His eyes widened in terror, and she desperately closed his wound.
			"[You'll be okay, dorogaya.]" she said softly, trying to calm him.
			He tried to speak, but blood spat from his mouth.
			She nearly finished stitching him, and then--BOOM!
			A shell, or a missile, or something else - she wasn't quite sure. The explosion rocked the ground beneath her feet. She knocked into the ground, rolled over, and checked mechanically to make sure her arm was still there - it was, but her shoulder had been dislocated. She looked over at the young man, whose wound was torn open by the blast. He was dead.
			She stood there for a moment, unable to think. Her brow furrowed, her pupils constricted, and then...
			She marched over, and grabbed the man's rifle. She tore off her medic patch - not that it had stopped them already. She clicked her shoulder back into place, readied the gun, grabbed a drum magazine, and charged.

			Meanwhile, just north of the AO, Trepov's forces were caught by separatists, and were stuck in a bloody battle with them, unable to support the convoy.
			Trepov ducked as a bomb went off near him. He looked around, and sprinted to his armoured car.
			Across the battlefield, Regimental Commissar Ivan Sokolov spotted him running.
			"[TREPOV!]" he roared. "[GET BACK HERE, YOU COWARD!]"
			"[The commander's leaving!]" one soldier shouted.
			"[We're doomed! We have to retreat!]" another cried.
			Ivan closed his eyes, tensed, and then opened. He looked through his rifle's iron sights, squinted, and fired a single bullet.
			Trepov's car spun out, crashed, and caught fire.
			Ivan leapt atop a tank hull, using the vantage point to take out separatist soldiers. He made himself a target, and got two bullets in the gut for his trouble. Undaunted, he kept firing.
			"[NOT ONE STEP BACK!]" he barked to his men. "[ONWARDS! FOR SOCIALISM! FOR DEMOCRACY! FOR THE SOVIET UNION!]"
			"[FOR THE UNION!]" his men roared back, renewed and wrathful. In moments, the separatists were the ones retreating.
			Ivan clambered atop the lead APC, and raised his gun in the air.
			"[Soldiers! Brothers and sisters of the USSR!]" he began. His comrades listened in to every word.
			"[A few miles from here, thousands of our comrades are being slaughtered by these traitors. We are their last hope of seeing the Red Dawn. NOW WHO'S WITH ME?!]"
			"[WE ARE!]" the soldiers barked back.
			"[THEN FOLLOW ME!]" he cheered, entering the vehicle.
			"[I--Commander!]" the driver began. "[You're bleeding - we need to get you to a medic.]"
			"[I'm fine!]" Ivan grinned, patching it up himself. "[Just drive the truck, comrade.]"

			Back in Lebedev's regiment, Sveta had 13 insurgent kills to her name. She was wrath incarnate - in a trance of blood.
			"[Die! Die, you traitorous bastards!]" she howled. A bullet landed in her leg. She buckled, ducked for cover, and fired back. She heard a satisfying *thump,* and grinned.
			Trepov's--well, Ivan's--regiment arrived, providing heavy artillery to scatter the rebels. Ivan ran out of the truck, and joined the fray. He spotted an enemy sniper, and sneaked around, before killing him. He grabbed the rifle, and saw the name "Isabella" scratched into it.
			"[Decent rifle... proper Dragunov, this...]" he mused, grinning. He looked through the scope, and was impressed by the quality. He pulled out his radio.
			"[All forces, this is Commissar Sokolov. I have just liberated a sniper rifle, and will be using it. Please don't blow up the nest I'm using - if you can help it.]"
			He chuckled, and spotted an enemy commander. He pulled the trigger, and he went down like paper.
			He kept doing this - and scores of rebels had their heads pop like grapes.
			Down in the carnage, Sveta spotted a rebel - he was a huge man, wearing bloodied kevlar. She shot at him, and he barely fliched.
			Unfazed, she kept firing, only for him to charge and launch her in the air. She landed down, and wheezed.
			"Poor girl." he said in English - he had an American accent.
			She pulled out her pistol, and fired at his head. It snapped back, but he didn't fall.

			Ivan clambered atop a wrecked vehicle - it wasn't clear if it was Soviet or rebel - and addressed his comrades-in-arms.

Tomorrow, we return to Moscow. And from there, we pay these rebel scum back, with interest! Long live the Soviet Union! On with the Red Dawn!]"

When our founding fathers came to this great country, we brought Africans with us. They performed the same function as the Slavs did to Rome, so we called them Slaves."

			Then his eyes turned, and looked over at the UK. He drew a circle over Drackhill.
			"You're next, my boy."

Likely, the mutations have confused their stem cells. That fits with my theory that their mutations are imperfect because their brain can't direct their generative cells properly."
			Jones nodded, stroking his chin. "What about the tests on pregnant rats?"
			Chloe shuddered slightly. "Injecting pregnant rats directly led to terminations of their pregnancies. Accepting the mutations makes you unable to bear children at all, it seems. As for in-utero exposure to the fetuses directly... Most of them simply spontanaeosly abort. A large number of the mother rats suffer severe aneurysms, too. It looks like serum-injected fetuses produce massive amounts of paradrenaline, which gets into the mother's system and causes the haemorrhaging. A couple of births have happened so far - all stillbirths... except for one."
			She showed him a tiny rat in an incubator. Despite all the other rats being albino as was common for lab-rats, including its parents - this one had healthy melanin levels.
			"Her mother died during birth, same as most. But she's the only one that survived in-utero exposure." she explained. "Rat pregnancies don't take long, and they give birth in litters - meaning we could produce several in a short amount of time. Still, there have been over 200 in-utero exposures, and she's the only one who survived."
			"Amazing..." Jones gasped. "Have you tested its DNA yet?"
			Chloe winced slightly at the use of 'It.' "No, not yet. She's still so fragile, I... I don't want to start taking samples until she gets a little bigger."
			"I understand..." Jones nodded. "But this has to be done. I'll take the sample - if anything goes wrong, it's my fault alone, okay?"
			Chloe sighed, but nodded silently, and left. Jones stuck a big needle into the tiny rat, and drew some blood into a vial.

It fired, taking that one down too. He morphed up his full suit, and re-created the ballistic shield from the bridge incident, before kicking the gate down.

If you didn't do what you did, then we'd still be together, in a relationship we both knew, deep down, wasn't working. I'm not going to lie and say I was the perfect boyfriend. 			Connor leant back, exhaling slowly. He hadn't expected closure to feel so... quiet. It wasn't the dramatic moment he'd imagined, but... maybe that was the point.

		SCENE
			That Wednesday, Connor and Sparky sat patiently on a plane. Ivan had a whiteboard with several notes on it. He stood and adressed the pair.
			"Another briefing?" Connor snarked.
			"Blah blah, Chechnya, blah blah, Russians, blah blah." Ivan jested back. "To summarise, Chechnya was conquered by the Timurids - a Turco-Mongol state in Iran - before Ivan the Terrible--"
			"You're not that bad!" Sparky barked, confused.
			"Thanks, tovarishch." Ivan grinned. "Anyway, the region wasn't fully annexed by the Russians until the rule of Peter the Great - that's when we expanded into the Caucasus. Typical colonial practices ensued - most notably, a mass deportation of over 80% of the Chechen and Ingush population during the 1860s and 70s. Anyway, skipping ahead a bit, following the October Revolution, Chechnya along with the rest of the Caucasus was re-integrated as part of the Greater Caucasian SFSR, which included Transcaucasia - places like Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan - and Ciscaucasia, where you'll find Ossetia, Dagestan, and relevant for us - Chechnya. And its current de-facto leader - Vadim Zamaldayev."
			He pointed to a photograph.
			"Zamaldayev was an influential general in the Ciscaucasian branch of the Red Army, having carved out his own petty fiefdom under Kruglov's idiocy. When things started getting unstable, he threw his lot in with the rebels, presenting himself as an Islamist militant in opposition to Soviet imperialism."
			"Imperialism? Any truth to the matter?" Connor cocked an eyebrow.
			"Before Kruglov? Not even an iota. After?" Ivan sighed heavily. "It hurts to say it, but we were acting like Capitalists under him. Not that Zamaldayev was a better man, but... that's not good enough."
			Connor smiled softly. Ivan took a deep breath, and continued.
			"I've told you a little about my run-in with him."
			"The battle of Grozny?" Connor tilted head.
			"That's the one. We managed to evacuate most Soviet Loyalists that day, but we lost the SFSR. We had to retreat to the Georgian SSR, and regroup. That's when I joined the KGB."
			"How have things been in Chechnya since then?"
			"There's a Turkic group called the Kumyks who live here - they and ethnic Russians make up the vast majority of non-Chechens here. Zamaldayev has taken to ethnically cleansing them. Currently, he's personally overseeing massacres."

			"Damn right. Okay, so - this is the plan. Anti-Zamaldayev forces have already started their attack on his position, but he's deployed Super-Agents. We go in, grab Zamaldayev. You kill his guards while I take him away. Sound good?"
			"Sounds good." Connor nodded. "Let's put this monster down."
			Sparky sat up. "I'm ready." he barked.
			"Okay... see you both on the ground!" Ivan shouted, running out the door. Connor and Sparky followed.

			Connor gripped Sparky hard, nuzzling him. They enjoyed the view.
			He regained his composure, and they morphed up their gliders as Ivan pulled his parachute chord. The trio landed in a small, abandoned village.
			"Okay, let's go. Do not kill Zalamdayev - he's ours." Ivan growled. With that, the trio descended.

			In the distance, the tyrant stood atop a tank, barking orders to his soldiers as they mowed down Kumyk fighters in cold blood. The massacre was brutal, the screams of the dying echoing across the open field. Zalamdayev's eyes gleamed with sadistic pleasure.

			Connor's blood boiled at the sight. His fists clenched, his jaw tightened, and before anyone could react, he leapt into the air, his body propelled by raw superhuman strength.
			He landed with a ground-shaking thud right in front of Zalamdayev's tank, his eyes glowing red.
			The Super-Agents around him snapped to attention, their guns drawn in a flash. Bullets rained down on Connor, the air around him crackling with the force of the barrage.
			He moved like a blur, his enhanced reflexes making him nearly untouchable, but some of the bullets managed to strike his body. The impact was heavy, but his healing factor kicked in almost instantly, the wounds knitting back together. Shrapnel from explosions embedded in his gut, tearing into his flesh, but he didn't even flinch. His rage drove him forward, and with a growl, he pulled the shards free, throwing them at the enemy like deadly projectiles.

			"No. Now we do things my way." the Commandant growled. "We need the data from your labs."
			"I will have it sent over, Commandant. It will take a few days to avoid audits, but..."
			"ENOUGH! Take him away."
			Morland begged for mercy as the guards dragged him out. A Super-Agent stepped forward. His black veins pulsed with mutant strength.
			"Agent Banner." the Commandant nodded.
			"Your orders, Commandant?" he asked.
			"Go to the labs. Take what we need, and cause a scene. Take the scientists hostage. I think I know who did this... You will take the one known as Chloe Derrington, and bring her away. Let our wayward friend come running to us."
			"As you wish, Commandant. Hail Victory." Banner nodded.
			"Hail Victory." the Commandant nodded back.

			That evening, Chloe was working in the lab with Jones.
			"Mondays, eh?" she smirked.
			"Did you hear?" he began. "Apparently the Werewolf was here a last night. Trashed the labs downstairs."
			"Wow, really?" Chloe asked, trying to act surprised. "That's crazy, I was here yesterday. What did he break?"
			"No idea. You know what downstairs are like - need to know, etc."
			"Hah, you can say that again." Chloe chuckled. With that, an alarm went off.
			"Shit - fire? Okay, let's go." Jones said hurriedly. Chloe nodded and left with him. They headed to the main hallway, where other staff had gathered, only to hear a noise - gunshots.
			"Fuck! Hide!" Jones barked, only for armed men to pour in.
			"NOBODY FUCKING MOVE!" the men roared. Banner approached. His eyes were even more blackveined than the average Super-Agent - a sign that this one had been twisted far beyond the norm.
			"Now, who here goes by the name Chloe Derrington?" he asked. No one answered.
			"No? Okay. Number 5, shoot that man there." he said. The other Agent readied his gun.
			"WAIT!" Chloe interrupted. "It's me. I'm Chloe Derrington."
			"Ah! Lovely to meet you at last. You're coming with me. The rest of you, my men will look after you." he grinned. His soldiers grabbed the other scientists and forced them to their knees. He dragged Chloe with him, heading up a flight of stairs.
			"Wh-where are you taking me?" she asked, trembling. She tried to steady her breath.
			"To the future, Crippled One." he laughed cruelly.

			At the same time, Connor was sat in the repair shop basement with the rest of the squad. He was on his laptop reviewing some files.
			"Oh, shit!" Shannon gasped.
			"What's up?" Connor tilted his head.
			"Reports just came in - there's an attack going on in Morland."
			"WHAT?!" Connor gasped.
			"Let's go." Sparky barked firmly.
			"Agreed." Amy nodded, rushing to her suit.
			"Amy... this'll be dangerous." Connor warned.
			"I don't care. If Chloe's in danger, I'm going." she snapped, drawing the Vibroblade.
			"That's not what I meant." he sighed. "There's a better way you can help?"
			"How?"
			Shannon approached, carrying a large, boxy device - it looked like a bulky handgun.
			"I call it the Pulsar." she explained. "We got the schematics off of a hack on Eidolon's servers. Anyway - it hooks up to your suit's battery. You can stun people at short range with it, softening them up for the others."
			She took it gingerly. Then her brows creased, and she nodded firmly.
			"You'd best get going." Shannon said. "Ivan's out of town at the moment - and Olivia's not on shift tonight. It's just you guys."
			"Let's do this." Sparky growled lowly.
			Amy finished suiting up, and hopped onto her motorbike.
			"I'll race you." she quipped, putting on her helm.
			Connor would normally snark back. Instead he nodded, and morphed his glider.

			As they moved, Connor felt his phone ring.
			"Connor! Look at the news!" Trey began.
			"I know! I'm on my way!"
			"Good man. Look, don't worry about your secret, okay? Just get there, and save Chloe."
			Connor paused for a split second. "I will." he vowed, and hung up. It rang again.
			"Connor! Chloe's in trouble!" Bea cried.
			"I'm heading there now!"
			"I'm stuck in traffic - they've blocked off Belson completely!"
			"I'm running there now - don't worry, Bea."
			"But what will you do?" she asked, shaking.
			"I don't know. But I'll do whatever I can."
			He hung up. Another phone call.
			"For fuck's sake..." he muttered before answering. "Hello?"
			"Bratan - big news."
			"Oh, hey Ivan - let me guess..."
			"Yes - Morland's under siege. Get there now. I'm in London at the moment - long story. I'll see you soon, tovarishch."
			Finally, Connor arrived. He felt his phone ringing, and looked at the scene - the entrance to the labs. DCI Naismith was there, ringing him. Upon spotting him, he hung up. Connor approached.
			"Werewolf." Naismith nodded. The armed officers in TO-24 aimed their guns at him.
			"Hold your fire!" he barked.
			"Sir?" DC Moffat asked. "But sir, he's... the Werewolf."
			"DC Moffat, stand down." Naismith replied. She hesitated, but put her gun down. Amy pulled up in her bike behind them.
			"Listen to me." Connor growled. "Inside that building are monsters beyond your capabilities. You go in there, it's a bloodbath - for everyone except the ones who need killing. Let me get in, I'll kill the Super-Agents, and you can rescue the humans."
			Naismith nodded. "10 minutes. After that, we're going in."
			"Got it." Connor replied, and headed inside.

			Upon entering, he saw the bodies of security guards who'd been shot. This wasn't America - security guards were unarmed. The Agents just wanted to kill someone. The heroes climbed the stairs.
			"Let's get these bastards." Sparky growled, his tail wafting in the air.
			The pair burst into a squad of Super-Agents. The Agents opened fire, but the heroes were on them in an instant.
			The fight was brutal. Connor ripped a knife from one Agent and used it to slit the man's throat before turning on another. Sparky tore through two more in one swipe.
			Amy charged forward, the bullets pinging and ricocheting off of her suit. She ripped out the Pulsar, and fired.
			Immediately, she felt it charge up. A ball of superpressurised air formed at the edge of the barrel, which shot forward. It slammed into the Agent, and he convulsed violently, before Sparky ripped off his head.
			Connor grabbed a grenade from a fallen Agent's belt, stuffing it into the man's mouth and kicking him into another, killing them both.
			Finally, a swipe from the Vibroblade opened a sucking hole on the last Agent's chest. Connor's punch went right through.
			With the carnage over, Connor dug a bullet from his hide, his breath ragged.
			"Sparky. Go downstairs. Kill them, and secure the labs. I'll go to the hostages." Connor ordered.
			Sparky barked in acknowledgment, running off to carry out his task.
			"Stunlocke - you okay?"
			She looked up. "Y-yeah."
			He gently approached. "Do you need to pull out?"
			"No. I need to kill these bastards."
			"Me too."
			They continued upward, finding the hostages knelt down in the hallway. As they stepped in, a Super-Agent revealed himself.
			"STOP RIGHT THERE!" he barked.
			Connor rushed past him, slamming into a soldier and spraying his guts on the ground.
			Amy's Pulsar stunned one, but a shotgun blast knocked her to the side. Connor sent his fist through the shooter, then his claw through another.
			One Agent got a lucky shot, and the bullet slammed into the side of Connor's head, sending him stumbling. A crossbow morphed from his wrist and he shot his attacker dead. He shook his head to clear the fog.
			"My god... you..." one of the scientists began.
			"Stay here. Are there any more hostages?" he asked, his voice trembling.
			"TRAITOR!" a voice screamed over the intercom - Banner's voice. "LISTEN AND OBEY!"
			At those words, Connor shuddered.
			"COME TO THE ROOFTOP. WE HAVE YOUR ACCOMPLICE." the voice boomed. "COME ALONE, OR SHE DIES."
			Connor's hearts stopped. He froze in place.
			A voice came over the intercom again. "Don't worry about me! Just save the people down below!" Chloe shouted. Her voice was interrupted by a thud and a yelp of pain.
			"HAH! SO NOBLE... NOW COME, OR SHE DIES!" the voice screamed again.
			Connor heard a ringing in his ears. Time slowed to a crawl. Hot blood poured from his nose. He shook his head.
			"I'm coming, Chloe." he whispered.

		Siege of Morland - Part 1

	Getting Closer
	______________________________
	CHAPTER
		______________________________
		SCENE
			Connor ascended the stairs, taking a moment to un-morph his mask and wipe his nose. The bullet to the head didn't crack his skull, but it still hurt.
			"Stunlocke - escort the hostages out of the reception. I'm going up." he said over the radio.
			"Copy that. I'll rejoin Predator once I'm done." she audibly nodded.
			"Vanguard - this is Whiplash. I took to the sky as soon as I heard the news."
			"You're a voice for sore ears." Connor smiled. "What's your status?"
			"I'm gliding over the roof. There's an Agent holding a girl at gunpoint. Want me to intervene?"
			"No - he'll kill her if anyone other than me shows up. Maintain aerial obs, but do not engage."
			"Copy that."
			He took a deep breath, re-morphed his mask, and headed up to the rooftop. There, he saw Banner, clad in armour, pointing his gun at Chloe.
			"Ah! Welcome back, Traitor!" he laughed.
			Connor responded by morphing a crossbow on his wrist, and aimed it directly at Banner's head. It was a message - if you hurt her, you will have half a second to regret it.
			"+*LET. HER. GO.*+" he roared, his voice slamming into Banner's chest like a sonic weapon.
			Chloe thought to herself - if that voice ordered her to jump from that rooftop, she would. She shook her head, glad that the voice was directed at Banner instead.
			Banner sneered, clearly rattled but not broken. He straightened, and chuckled darkly. "Hah... Nice try."
			He holstered his weapon with a deliberate slowness, as if dismissing Connor's power. "You think you can intimidate me with your little tricks? Come then, Traitor - show me Paladin's wrath!"
			Connor's eyes glowed a deep, furious red, the power of the Rage flooding his veins. His muscles tightened, rippling with supernatural strength. His voice boomed again, louder this time, shaking the very air around them. "+*PALADIN GAVE ME MY _STRENGTH_*+" he roared. The ground beneath them seemed to tremble as the force of his words resonated. "+*THE WRATH... IS _MINE ALONE_!*+"
			With a primal roar, he charged. He threw a punch with such force that the air seemed to crack around it - aided, no doubt, by Olivia's power from above. Banner barely managed to block, but the impact sent him sliding back. Connor pressed the attack, launching another punch, then a devastating uppercut that could take a human's head off. Each swing felt like it could tear through steel, each blow a promise of death.
			Chloe looked on, horrified and transfixed by the scene. But only one thought was in her mind.
			In his rage, Connor didn't bother to hide his voice. Sure, he may have been shouting with a supernatural growl, but still...
			"That voice..." she whispered, trembling - not wanting to realise the implications.
			Banner was no amateur. He was fast, and brutal. He counterattacked with a kick so vicious it seemed to explode from his body.
			The impact landed directly in Connor's chest, and a sickening crunch filled the air. The force knocked him back, and he stumbled, gasping for air. Blood dripped from his mouth.
			Chloe, her heart pounding, saw an opportunity. She tried to run, but in a split second, Banner's hand whipped out, throwing a knife with deadly precision. It sailed through the air towards her. Time seemed to slow as she twisted, barely avoiding the blade. It was a sign to stay put.
			Connor's Rage flared. His fists, still trembling from the blow, morphed out a blade. With a guttural roar, he lunged, stabbing Banner in the thigh. The blade sank deep, but Banner grinned through the pain. He grabbed the blade and twisted it free. Without hesitation, he plunged it into Connor's abdomen.
			The agony was unbearable - Connor could feel the blade scrape against his ribs, tearing through muscle and flesh. Blood poured from the wound, but his resolve only hardened.
			Undaunted, he gritted his teeth, his fingers tightening around Banner's blade. With a feral snarl, he shifted, forcing himself forward along the blade. The two warriors were locked in a brutal embrace, each one trying to kill the other. Connor morphed claws on his hands, slashing wildly. Banner screamed as the blades cut across his face, sending a spray of blood into the air. He staggered back, but Connor followed, relentless.
			He gripped the blade from his chest. He had to finish this. He had to save Chloe. His constant humming migraine faded for a moment - even his flesh wanted this man dead.
			He pulled the blade from his chest, as Banner jumped on his back. He ran himself through, impaling both.
			For a moment, there was silence, save for the ragged breaths of two men on the verge of death. Blood pooled around them, dark and thick.
			They both fell away from each other, and struggled to stand up, blood pouring from their chests and mouths. Connor planted the blade in the ground, and used it to help him stand.
			Chloe rushed to him, her eyes wide with horror and relief. She helped him to his feet, but just as they thought they had a moment of calm, Banner drew his gun again, aiming it directly at her head. 
			"Ah, ah, ah!" Banner laughed. He motioned for Chloe to step away, and she reluctantly did so. Connor growled, like a true Werewolf.
			Banner approached and grabbed her, holding the gun to her head.
			"Nice try. But the heart always was your weakness, traitor." he laughed. "On your knees."
			Connor sank down. 
			"Now..." Banner smirked. "Take off your mask."
			Connor shuddered. Chloe gulped.
			"No... Don't... It... it can't be..." she stammered, knowing deep down what she'd see. "I don't want to know." she whispered. "Don't be Connor... Don't be Connor..."
			"Oh, but it is. Come on, traitor. Listen and Obey." Banner grinned.
			Connor slowly raised his hands, and pulled down his mask. The colour drained from Chloe's face as she saw him.
			"...Connor?" she asked, choking back tears.
			"I... I'm sorry..." he admitted, unable to look her in the eyes.
			"See him! See how he lies! The wayward son of our master. Misbegotten. A failure. You were meant to be one of us, Connor! A perfect specimen. How dare you betray your own kind!" Banner laughed.
			With that, Chloe sprang into action. Remembering Connor's training, she grabbed Banner's wrist, launched his arm into the air, and shoved. His grip was too tight for him to let go of the gun, but he stumbled, towards the edge of the roof.
			"Filthy cripple!" he roared, aiming his gun at her.
			"NO!" Connor bellowed, launching himself.
			Banner pulled the trigger just a second before Connor slammed into his torso. Both men careened off the edge. The bullet veered off course, skimming past her face. Olivia tried her hardest to catch Connor, too.
			Chloe froze for a moment. As the two fell, Banner shot at Connor in the air. She ran to the edge, and saw them hit the ground together. A thud... a sickening thud. She fell to her knees.
			"Connor... CONNOR!" she screamed.
			She ran down the stairs, as fast as her legs could take her.
			She heard gunshots - the police had swarmed the building now, to rescue the hostages. She'd have to be quick...
			She darted past them, and found her way to the alleyway Connor landed. The same alleyway he and Sparky saved her from all those months ago. There, she saw Banner - or what was left of him. He landed right on his head, and a pile of red mush was all that remained above his neck.
			But Connor... Connor landed back-first on a dumpster. He was bent backwards in a sickening, unnatural way - his back was snapped clean in half. Chloe fell down to her knees again.
			"No... NO!" she sobbed. She pulled his body from the dumpster, laying him down flat. He didn't breathe.
			"Connor... Connor, wake up. Come on, wake up. Please wake up... Hey, remember this alleyway? You saved me here, and you just saved me again. Come on... Come on, get up! That's an order!" she pleaded. She slammed his chest with her fist, causing a cracking noise from his spine.
			"Come on, get up... Hey, if you get up, I'll... I'll forgive you, okay? I won't be mad, not even a little. Just... please wake up. You've survived so much, you can survive this! Please!" she sobbed. "Please..." she begged, as she hit his chest again. Another cracking noise. With that...
			"GAAGGH!" Connor gasped, his eyes shooting open.
			"Connor?!" she looked up.
			"Agh... AAAGH!" he screamed in agony. He rolled onto his front and clutched his back.
			"Connor... Connor, what... What do I do?" she asked, tears streaming down her cheek.
			"Agh... Ah... I... Help..." he spluttered out, trying to stand. Chloe helped him up. He shouted in pain as he rose, but found his footing.
			"Connor, you... You're alive..." she whispered, in shock.
			With that, the police exited the building. "Area secure, sir!" Nina barked. "All hostages save one have been located. Captive hostile has been subdued."
			"I..." Chloe began. "You'd better go. If they find you..."
			"Chloe, I..." Connor started, but she raised her hand, silencing him.
			"We'll talk about this later, okay? I... I'll see you later." she said, and hugged him. Though his back was in agony, he hugged her too.
			"The cops will wanna question you." he choked. "When they're done, get them to drop you off at the repair shop. I'll explain everything, I promise."
			She nodded hesitantly, and he hobbled off into the distance.

		Siege of Morland - Part 2
		______________________________

			An hour later, Chloe was in the police interview room. Nina was sat with her.
			"They shouldn't be much longer... Can I get you a drink or anything?" she asked.
			"Um... Just water, please." Chloe said, still in shock. Nina nodded, and fetched a glass of water. With that, DC Moffat and DCI Naismith entered.
			"Sorry about the delay." Naismith began. "Can I get you anything before we begin, Chloe?"
			"No thank you... I, um, I have water."
			Naismith nodded, and pressed the recording button on the tape. "TO-24 Interview of Miss Chloe Derrington, by DCI Henry Naismith, DC Cheryl Moffat, and PS Nina Chowdhury. Please state your names for the tape."
			"DC Moffat."
			"PS Chowdhury."
			"Chloe Derrington."
			"DCI Naismith. Now, Chloe, before we get started, I want to make it clear that you are being interviewed as a witness, not a suspect in any criminal matter. You are not under caution, nor in any trouble. You can say 'no comment' to any of my questions, and we can stop the interview at any time. Is that all clear?" he asked.
			"Yes." Chloe nodded, looking into the distance.
			"Excellent. Now, it would help us if you could give us a rough timeline of events." he smiled. "Take your time."
			"Okay... Um, so, I was working in the lab with Jones--uh, that is, Mr. Peter Jones. We heard the alarm go off... I want to say around 7:30? Anyway, we went into the hallway where the other scientists had gathered, when we heard the gunshots..." Chloe shuddered. "Then, they came barging in, and one of them, he was wearing armour. He threatened to shoot people if I didn't go with him, so I went along with him."
			"That was very brave of you." Nina said, smiling warmly at her.
			"And when you went with him, he took you to the rooftop, and held you at gunpoint - is that correct?" Naismith asked.
			"Yes, that's correct." Chloe nodded.
			"Right..." Naismith searched through his documents. "According to witness testimony, when the Werewolf entered the building, your captor took control of the intercom, and demanded that he come and face him. Is that correct?"
			"Yeah, that's right. He, um..." Chloe paused, not wanting to reveal Connor's - or her - involvement. "He told the Werewolf that he'd kill me unless he came there immediately, and alone."
			"Right... And when he came up, what happened?"
			"They fought. It was... At one point, the Werewolf drew a blade, and stabbed the man with it. The man just took the blade and ran him through. Then, the Werewolf slashed his face, and..." she shuddered at the memory.
			"You're doing very well, Chloe." Moffat smiled. Chloe nodded.
			"They ended up in a scuffle. The man was jumped on the Werewolf's back. So he... He basically committed Seppuku."
			"He impaled himself, and the other man?" Naismith asked.
			"Yes." she said, closing her eyes for a moment.
			Naismith's face softened for a moment. "You've been through a lot, Chloe. I know this isn't easy, but you're doing great."
			"And what happened after that?" Moffat asked.
			"He, um... I helped the Werewolf back up to his feet. He was injured, and, well, he was saving me, so..." Chloe looked away.
			"No one's going to question your decision there." Naismith smiled.
			Chloe nodded, and continued. "The man... he drew his gun again, and grabbed me. Held me at gunpoint again. I think he knew he was losing, so he wanted an out."
			"And what happened next?"
			Chloe's mind flashed - Connor's face under the mask. She banished the thought - she *could not* tell them.
			"I... I tried to disarm him. My boyfriend, he... he teaches me martial arts. I grabbed the man's wrist, and pushed him back. But he was too strong - he held on to the gun. He aimed at me, and as he fired, the Werewolf pushed him off the rooftop... they both fell."
			"Is that where you got the injury on your face from?" Naismith asked, pointing to the cut on her cheek.
			"Yeah... the bullet just missed me. I think it grazed my cheek." she nodded, touching the cut, and running her finger over her older scar beneath.
			"So, after that... We found you in the alleyway, next to the Agent's body." Moffat began.
			"Yes, I... I ran down the stairs to see what had happened. I... I wasn't thinking straight." Chloe replied.
			"Well, he had saved your life. It's only natural to want to check on him." Nina added, smiling sympathetically.
			Chloe cleared her throat. "I made it to the alleyway, and found both bodies. The Werewolf - his back was snapped. He was... slumped over backwards..."
			"But his body was missing - did he survive?" Naismith asked, eager for information.
			"He, um... I pulled his body down and laid it flat. I... I just planned to give CPR. But he got up, and..." her mind flashed to Connor's agony again.
			"He was in pain. So, I helped him up, and then he left. I... I didn't see where he went." she finished.
			"That all checks out..." Naismith said, reviewing his notes. "Well, Chloe - you're free to go. We'll contact you if we need anything. Morland will be closed for the time being - I'm sure your boss will let you know once we've cleared out."

			"Interview terminated at 22:28." Moffat nodded, switching off the recorder.
			"Chloe, do you need a lift home?" Nina asked.
			"I, um... yes please." Chloe replied.
			With that, Nina took Chloe to her car.
			"Where to?"
			"Riverside Repairs, Redbridge." she answered.

			Nina's car pulled up outside the repair shop. Chloe took a deep breath.

			"No. I was born here, moved to Derry as a baby, and moved back here at 7. Everything I've told you about my life is true. My sister is still Amy, and my uncle is still Vince. I still met Trey when I was 15, and I still... I still met you. That's all true."

			"No. I... I'd just got these powers, and I wanted to figure out how they worked."
			"When did you get them? And how?"
			"I was abducted, about a week and a half before we met. They... shot me. And then they must have brought me back. My guess is, they injected me with as much serum as they could. Maybe they wanted to see how much they could give someone without killing them. Anyway, they got more than they bargained for. I am to them what they are to humans."
			"So the whole time I've known you, you've had this... this double life?" she asked.
			"I--yes." he nodded, ashamed.
			"Was any of it real?"
			"W-what do you mean?" he asked.
			"When I was jumped outside my work. Was that all part of the lie?"
			"No, god no!" he shook his head. "I mean, yes, I lied when I said I was nearby - I sprinted over rooftops to get to you - but I didn't set that up. I would never!"
			"How many people have you killed?"
			"Chloe..." Connor began, uncomfortable.
			"Tell me. How many." she asked, firmly.
			"158." he finally admitted.
			Chloe gasped. "And why did you kill them?" she finally said.
			"The Super-Agents, because there's no safe way to let them live. The humans... most of them were collateral damage. I was lost in the Rage, and they were attacking me - it was instinct. There are 3 normal humans I killed of my own free will." Connor explained, studying her reaction. "Omar Hattab - a Algerian general plotting a war. Alan Hughes - a perv who sold kids. And Vadim Zamaldayev - a Chechen warlord."
			At the final mention, she looked surprised. "You killed Zamaldayev?"
			"You know about him?"
			"Yeah, he... Sveta was injured fighting against his group. She told me stories about him..." Chloe trailed off, deep in thought. For all her fears and rage, killing Zamaldayev was justified.
			"Do you remember how last Wednesday, you wanted to meet up, but I said I was busy? I was in Chechnya at the time." he explained. "I got pretty badly hurt - lost my arm and half my gut. I was still aching on the open day, but I'd mostly healed up by that point."
			Chloe's stomach twisted. "How do you live with that?"
			"It wasn't easy. I looked fine, but the damage was mainly internal."
			"No, I mean..." she shook her head. "How do you cope with 158 kills?"
			Connor rubbed his temples, as if the weight of it all was physically pressing on him.
			"I didn't want to kill them. But when you're forced into a corner, when they give you no choice... it's not always as clear-cut as we want it to be."
			"Who else knows?" she asked. "Who else knew my boyfriend was a superhero before me?"
			"...my team."

		SCENE
			That night, Connor was sprinting, leaping from rooftop to rooftop in a patrol. While running, he heard a scream. He sprinted straight towards the source.
			There, he saw a monster grabbing a man in Patriot leathers. The monster let the man go, and turned to face Connor.
			It was a freak that would make Nosferatu look pretty. Its skin was grey, and its eyes a dark blood-red, blending iris, pupil, and sclera. Its face was only vaguely human - its eyes too far apart, its nose at once too pointy and too flat, its jaw stuttered and spiked. All in all, it could only be described by negation - "Face not-quite-human," "Teeth not-quite-canine," "Frame not-quite-apelike."
			"This is Vanguard. Contact." he whispered in shock.
			The creature turned slowly, its face twisted into a grotesque grin.
			"Greetings, youngblood." it growled, lips curling. "Are you ready for your judgment?"
			Connor raised an eyebrow, taking a step forward. His usual cocky smirk formed. "Who the fuck are you?"
			"I am the Judge." the creature replied, showing its teeth, the grin stretching impossibly wide. "And I am your end, youngblood."
			Connor's smirk deepened. "Oh? Well, if you'll let me be the 'judge' for a second - I find you guilty of being fuck-ugly."
			The Judge's grin faltered for a moment, but then it returned, colder than before. "Such insolence, to curse and demean your natural ruler. Your death has been demanded - thus sayeth the Lord."
			"'The Lord'? You mean the Commandant?" Connor asked, eyebrow raised.
			"Do not dare blaspheme in such ways." the Judge snarled, his voice venomous. "To compare the Lord to the Commandant is to compare a star to a single ember."
			Connor tilted his head, genuinely curious now. "Who were you? What, a preacher?"
			The Judge's eyes narrowed, a cold flicker passing through them. "No. You are mistaken. I do not come to bring the Word to the ears of mankind. I am the Judge. And I find you... guilty."
			His voice hardened, and his grip tightened on his weapons.
			Connor pressed, determined to understand. "But who *were* you?" He gestured toward the creature's horrific form, his voice tinged with real concern.
			The Judge's eyes flared. "Be silent." he snapped, his voice sharp. "Mine eyes have been opened by the Lord, heretic. Do not dare labour under the delusion that you can close them once more."
			Connor stared at him, his expression hardening. "Have it your way." he muttered, his eyes flashing. He morphed his blades, their gleaming edges catching the light. "Let's dance."
			The Judge's grin widened. "I hereby sentence you to death." he said grimly. "May the Lord burn your soul for eternity."
			Without another word, they charged.

			The sound of their blades clashing rang out in the alley as the two monsters collided. The first thing Connor noticed was the Judge's strength - far greater than he expected. The creature moved with unnatural speed, his strikes heavy and relentless. Connor was forced to backpedal, his blades deflecting each blow.
			The Judge struck again, and this time, Connor's parry was too slow. The Judge's blade cut deep into Connor's thigh. Blood poured from the wound.
			Connor swung his blade with a growl, his edge slicing across the Judge's thigh. The creature howled in pain, stumbling back slightly, but the grin never left its face.
			The Judge's next move was swift - he brought his blade down toward Connor's head. Connor reacted instinctively, diving backward, barely avoiding the blow. He threw a knife, but the creature was too fast, parrying the blade with one of its own. The two made eye contact - two predators circling each other, their blades hungry for blood.
			"About time for a challenge." Connor thought, the adrenaline surging through him. His fear was buried deep, hidden beneath the hunger for battle.
			The Judge didn't waste time. He plunged his blade into the ground, sending a shockwave of energy through the earth. The pavement cracked, and gravel flew into the air. With a growl, the Judge charged forward, sweeping his blade up. The gravel cut into Connor's eyes, blinding him momentarily.
			Connor staggered back, wiping the dirt from his eyes, but the Judge was already on him. The second flurry of strikes came fast, and one of them finally landed - cutting across Connor's abdomen. The pain was immediate, sharp, and deep. Blood poured from the wound, but Connor forced himself to focus.
			With a roar, he swung his longblade, the strike strong enough to send a shockwave through the Judge's defenses. The creature blocked the attack, but Connor grinned. It was a feint. He thrusted his shortblade forward, burying it deep into the Judge's abdomen.
			But the Judge didn't falter. His grin only grew wider as he grabbed Connor's blade and pushed it out, his other hand moving faster than Connor could react. In a single fluid motion, the Judge morphed his blades into a spear, thrusting it toward Connor. The weapon drove into his abdomen with brutal force.
			Connor grabbed the spear, pulling himself toward the Judge with a snarl. He morphed blades from his wrists, slashing at the Judge's face. The strike connected, cutting deep, but the Judge simply grinned. He twisted the spear, and Connor felt the blade tear through his insides, sending shockwaves of agony through his body.
			For the first time since starting his quest, real, primal fear crept into Connor's hearts. The blood loss, the agony, the damage...
			Thoughts flooded his mind. His friends. His pack. He couldn't die here. Not like this.
			The Judge morphed his spear back into twin blades, spinning them in the air like a tornado of death. Connor tried to stand his ground, but his legs betrayed him. He was on the edge of collapse.
			Then, with a deafening howl, Connor's eyes flashed red. Rage. The bloodlust took over, drowning out the pain, drowning out the fear. His body surged with raw power, and his vision turned crimson.
			The Judge wiped blood from his mouth, his grin widening. "Now... Now it's a fight." he muttered, his own eyes flashing red with a sudden, dangerous fury. He un-morphed his blades, drawing wristblades in their place.
			The two monsters collided again. Their wristblades clashed in a shower of gore, neither one attempting to block - only strike. Blood splattered across the alley as their bodies were torn. For a moment, the Judge stumbled, his left hand pressing against the stab wound Connor inflicted earlier. But his grin only grew fiercer, and his eyes glowed red.
			For a split second, Connor's mind cleared. "He can Rage too?" The thought barely registered before his feral instincts took over once more. The two continued to clash, a blur of violence and blood.
			The Judge hit harder than anyone Connor had faced before. Each strike felt like it could shatter bone, and Connor was barely able to stay on his feet. But he fought through the pain, launching a haymaker that connected with the Judge's ribcage. He felt something crack beneath his fist.
			For a moment, the Judge faltered, his breath ragged. He straightened, his body obeying his will with terrifying precision.
			Connor didn't realise his mistake until it was too late.
			The Judge swiped, his blade slashing across Connor's throat with terrifying precision. Before he could react, the Judge grabbed his tongue, yanking it out with a sickening pull.
			Then, in one fluid motion, the Judge re-morphed his spear, driving it through Connor's chest.
			Connor howled, the sound tearing from his chest as the spear twisted, shredding his lungs. Blood poured from him in torrents as the Judge raised the spear into the air, a triumphant roar echoing in the alley. His left heart was completely punched out, and his right was horribly mangled to the point of unusability.
			With a brutal, final motion, the Judge drove the spear into the ground, impaling Connor like a trophy.
			Connor's limp body slumped down, blood pooling around him. The Judge stood over him, his eyes returning to their cold, fanatical calm. He chuckled, the sound dark and victorious. He placed a hand on Connor's chin, almost gently.
			"You fought well, youngblood. Though you squander the gifts of the Great One... you fought well."
			Connor tried to speak, to roar, to spit. Something.
			"Shh..." the Judge replied, again with a horrifyingly gentle tone. "Don't be ashamed. You did your best. Nothing that happens after today is your fault."
			Again, another death-rattle came out of Connor's bloody mouth.
			"Hush, now, youngblood." the Judge smiled - not savagely, but warmly - "Go in peace."

			With that, the Judge rose, bowed, and left.
			Connor's limp, apparently lifeless body slid down the spear, making a sickening *squelch* as it hit the ground.
			Must hold on. Must hold on.
			Every cell in Connor's body screamed. Every nerve ending begged him to just let them die.
			Must hold on. Must hold on.
			No oxygen. Only a torn heart for circulation.
			Must hold on. Must hold on.
			Bleeding from every organ. Brain... shutting down...
			Must... hold on...

	Judgement Day
	______________________________
	CHAPTER

		FLASHBACK
			It was early hours of the 24th of October, 1996. 03:27 AM.
			A Thursday. The 49th United Nations day, specifically.
			There was a light spatter of rain, but the night sky wasn't too cloudy. Were it not for the city's light pollution, you'd be able to see the night stars with impressive clarity.
			The moon was a waxing gibbous - nearly full.
			And one man remembers all of this. Every detail. He can't forget it.
			No matter how much he wants to.

			Vince's car swerved into the hospital car park, narrowly missing a bollard. Without bothering to straighten into the lines, he burst out of his door, and sprinted like a blur over to the passenger side. He swung the door open, nearly pulling it off its hinges, and pulled his sister Laura from the seat. She was pale, and struggled to keep her eyes open. Blood and amniotic fluid coated her legs.
			"Vince..." she whispered through ragged breaths. "Something... Something's not right..."
			"Shh..." he replied, carrying her to the hospital entrance. "You'll be alright..."
			He made it to the door, kicked it open, and screamed for help.

			Roughly an hour had passed.
			Specifically, it was now 04:42 AM. The clouds had begun to draw in, and the rain was becoming a little stronger. The moon peeked out through the clouds, as though it was too scared to watch.
			Vince anxiously paced the hospital corridors, as Laura's screams filled his ears. A nurse approached him, her face pale.
			"M-mister Barrett?" she asked.
			"Is she okay?" he hurriedly answered, rushing over.
			"There... there seems to be a problem." the nurse admitted. "Laura is suffering from an acute brain haemorrhage."
			"Oh, God..." Vince whispered in shock. "Is... is there anything you can do?"
			"At the moment, we have two options." the nurse began. "We can provide her with medication to stem the blood flow and give her time to recover. However, this medication... it'd be toxic to the baby."
			Vince ran his hands through his hair.
			"Our other option... would be to perform a C-section right away, and try to save the baby. But the additional blood loss... Laura would most likely die."
			Vince agonised over the choice for less than a second. It felt like hours.
			"Save her." he nodded, closing his eyes.
			"Are you sure?" the nurse asked.
			"I'm sure. Save her. Please..." he begged.
			The nurse nodded, and left.

			27 minutes later, the nurse returned.
			"I..." she began, struggling to find the words. "I'm so sorry, Mr. Barrett."
			"No..." he whispered, burying his face in his hands.
			"We did everything we could, but... Laura didn't make it."
			The words echoed in his brain.
			"Can I... Can I see her, please?" he finally asked.
			"Of course." the nurse nodded, ushering him into her room.
			He sat by her side, and squeezed her hand. She was pale and still.
			Vince had always assumed that people would look peaceful in death. But she didn't look peaceful. Her face was still slightly contorted from the pain. Her skin was cold and damp to the touch.
			Vince wept. He howled in pain and sorrow.
			He rested his hand on her abdomen, and...
			He felt movement.
			Kicking. Punching. Flailing, perhaps.
			"NURSE!" he screamed.

			13 minutes had passed, and the nurse arrived - carrying a newborn baby.
			Vince took him into his arms. He looked into the little one's eyes. Icy, steel grey. Pale skin.

		Getting Connor to A&E

But it's the best I can do. My life... It doesn't matter compared to that."
			"It matters to me!" Chloe replied, teary eyed. "Why do you have to be the hero?!"
			"Because it's the right thing to do." he said, rising to his feet. He pulled off the monitoring equipment, and morphed up his costume. The costume struggled to form, but managed to cover him once more.
			"Connor... I am begging, *begging* you. You cannot do this--" she pleaded, but Connor cut her off.
			"I have to do this!"
			"LISTEN TO ME!" she barked. "You cannot do this *alone.* And you wanna know something? You're not alone."
			Sparky jumped up, licking Connor's face. "You're not alone. You have us all."
			Ivan nodded. "I'm with you until the end, bratan."
			"Damn right." Olivia nodded.
			Connor sat back down on the bed, and sighed. He reached his hand into his chest, and rubbed his growing heart.
			"Now..." Chloe began, taking a deep breath. "I've been going over your body ever since the fight. The Judge must be stronger than you, or at least of comparable strength. However, it looks like... I can't explain it, but while you were in the coma, your muscle density nearly doubled. Maybe, when you suffer near-fatal trauma, your body rebuilds itself stronger than before."
			Connor looked at her, deep in thought. "So, you're saying... I'm stronger?"
			"Yes, but don't get cocky. Just because you're stronger doesn't mean you're invincible."
			"I underestimated the Judge once. I will *not* let that happen again." Connor vowed.
			"Also - I was looking at your cells after you were brought here. It's... remarkable. Your body simply refused to die." she said, astonished.

			"I mean, your non-essential cells entered dormant states to avoid using up energy - and, for the record, the cells your body considers 'non-essential' is pretty revealing on its own. Practically everything except your amygdala, your backup heart, and your bone marrow, was all shut down. The lactic acid buildup you had - it would have caused any human cell to enter apoptosis almost immediately. But yours just kept on going. You've, um... You've had some damage to the amygdala, but that's mostly healed now. Still, your reflexes and motor control will be impaired somewhat."

			"Healing - but you're in a bad way, Connor. You can't fight like this."

			"I'll fight with you. I'll harass this 'Judge' while you go in for the kill. Just... be careful, okay?"

			"I'll provide telekinetic support." Olivia nodded. "Make your hits harder, and his veer off."
			"And my Pulsar should give you some openings." Amy added. "We can do this if we all go together."
			"...I guess me and Shan can provide moral support." Trey snarked.
			"We've been working on some improvements for Amy's suit." Shannon smiled. "We'll retrofit them on right away."
			Connor smiled softly. He looked up at Chloe.
			"Connor..." she began.
			"Guys... can you give me and Chloe a minute?" Connor asked. They all nodded, and left.
			
			Chloe sat on the bed, next to Connor.
			He put his arm around her, and she hugged into him, and began to cry.
			"I'm sorry..." he began.
			"Do you even realise how fragile you looked lying here? For once, you weren't indestructible. You weren't a hero. You were just... you. And I was terrified I wouldn't get you back."
			"I know... And I hate the thought of making you scared. But... I have a mission. These monsters will keep killing people - and their victims stay dead."
			"I thought I'd lost you. How often do you get hurt this badly?" she asked.
			"This has been one of the rougher weeks." Connor quipped. "Sorry, bad time for a joke."
			Chloe chuckled anyway, allowing the moment.
			"So, um... Three days. How's the city been?"
			"There's been a few more attacks. Ivan's had the others benched for the time being, but people haven't realised yet. There's rumours that the string-ups were one of you guys, so common criminals are afraid you've started killing them, too."
			"Fuck... that's very bad." Connor shuddered. "How's Bea been?"
			"I told her you're away for work, with no signal. And I said I've been transferred to a new lab here in the hospital. I... I hate lying to her." she admitted. "She's worried, though. About the city, and... well, she can tell that we're all upset."
			"...I'm sorry for making you lie. Once this is done... I'm done with the lies."
			Chloe hugged him tightly. "You don't have to do this, Connor."
			"I know I don't." he nodded. "But if you could do what I can, wouldn't you do this?"
			Chloe paused, and sighed. "I can't fault you for that. I... I suppose I would. Just..." she took a moment, and placed her hand on his heart - more literally than usual.
			"I hate that I understand why you do this. I hate that I see the person you are - the person who would sacrifice everything to protect others - and I know I'd never ask you to change. I wish you never got these powers of yours - but you do have them. And that means you have a responsibility to use them. And if you weren't the kind of guy to feel that way, then I probably never would have fallen in---" she caught herself. It was harder to spit it out when he was awake. "...Fallen for you. But it doesn't make this any easier, Connor." she said. "I'm torn. I feel angry that you're out there risking your life, guilty for me being so selfish... When I'm with you, I feel... I feel like I'm keeping you away from the people who need you, who *really* need you. But... *I* need you! And I'm useless to you."
			"You're not." Connor replied firmly. "You... my time with you is what keeps me human. If I didn't have you, if I was the Werewolf all the time, well... I wouldn't be Connor. I'd be no different to Paladin - a killing machine. The only difference would be who I kill, and what for."
			"I..." Chloe began. "I just feel so powerless watching you fight, knowing I can only help from the sidelines. I can't fight these things! I can study you, but what good am I from here?"
			"I have an idea." Connor tilted his head. "I know what you're like - you took a look at the paradrenaline in my system, right?"
			"Yeah - I was trying to find a way to stimulate it to help you heal quicker." she replied.
			"And did you find anything else?"
			"I... yes!" Chloe said, realising. "Hang on..." 
			She went through the notes she'd taken through the process. "Here! The endorphin-analogue that counteracts the paradrenaline. Your body kept almost rinsing your head with it - thank god it did, or you'd have had a seizure, or a stroke. In fact, I think this substance is what put you in the healing coma."
			She showed him the paperwork. As she explained, her demeanour shifted - more confident, less vulnerable. This was her element.
			"EEGs showed you were in severe pain - so we tried giving you anaesthetics, but your body just metabolised them instantly. It's all a part of this intracellular communication you seem to have - your body recognises when a substance has foreign origins, and immediately moves to neutralise, expel, or digest it. But..."
			She turned the page, and pulled out a syringe.
			"This stuff here." she pointed. "The endorphin analogue. Because I synthesised it from your own endocrine system, your body recognised it as coming from itself. So I cooked up a high enough dose, and that seemed to calm you down a notch. Slight problem though - it's brought your paradrenaline way down. I'd need to synthesise more if you wanted to use your Rage."
			Connor paused, deep in thought. "So... that's the substance that counters the paradrenaline? And can you synthesise more of it?"
			"Yes - in a couple hours, I could make a full dose."
			Realisation dawned on his face. "The Judge will be out again in a few hours. Before we head out, can you make enough paradrenaline to trigger the Rage? And... a full dose of the endorphins?"
			"Yeah, absolutely. I'll crack on now." Chloe said, brushing away her tears and squaring her shoulders.
			Connor rose, a soft smile breaking through the pain on his face. He pulled Chloe into a hug, holding her tightly. She returned the embrace, not wanting it to end.
			She swallowed hard, resting her forehead against his. "Rest while you can. I'll handle this."
			Connor nodded, stepping back. As he laid back down, Chloe sat at her makeshift lab station, her hands trembling for only a moment before she steadied them. She glanced back at him, then down at her notes. Her jaw set with quiet determination.

			He charged, deliving a flurry of heavy jabs to Junior's torso. Junior seemed unfazed, and then backhanded Connor with enough force to launch him through the wall and into the street outside.

			The Judge was a killing machine, but he had weaknesses to exploit.
			What the fuck was this thing?!
			He looked down, and saw blood. Not his. He stood, and realised he'd been launched straight into the barman, crushing him to death.
			he winced, and morphed out his blades, just as Junior came rushing out on all fours.
			He braced for impact.

			"Ugh, can't wait to be done with this module." Bea grinned.
			"You and me, both." Chloe chuckled.

			"Fire, perhaps?" Bea tilted her head.
			"No, it's an announcement." Chloe stroked her chin. The ringing stopped, and the announcer began.

			"...until this is over, we urge everyone to stay indoors, and to stay away from Belson." the newscaster said. Behind him was live footage - of Junior fighting Connor.
			The girls went deathly pale.

			Sparky pounced out from the rubble, his eyes aflame with Rage. He cut into Junior's back, drawing blood.
			Not enough to hurt it. Only enough to piss it off.
			Junior swung around, then began beating Sparky like a chimp, flailing its arms down wildly.
			Connor rose up with something approaching consciousness, drenched in his own blood.
			His vision was blurry, but he could see what that monster was doing to his packmate.

			"I'm fine..." Sparky nodded. "What is this thing?"

			"You saw that thing... it was huge!"

			"We've gotta help him." Amy said firmly. "Now."

I can cook up some things... Paradrenaline, endorphins, xeno-grehlin... he'll need those to recover. So will Sparky."

			"Come on - no time like the present." Bea nodded. Amy swallowed, and they moved.

Then, it ripped out a street light, and, swinging the rebar like a club, whacked Connor across the side of the head. Sparky landed across the street, dazed.

His body sprawled out as it hit into the ground, with a noticable pothole forming as his face smacked down. He forced himself to rise, to fight, to not die, and a second swing around the side of the head sent him flying back into the cracked, crumbling building.

			The funny thing about super senses is, they tell you things that you might not think are important.
			For example, Connor didn't even think twice about the wall being load-bearing. Especially not when, as he hit the wall, the force of repeated impacts and the cracks in his skull meant his right eye had been dislodged. His armour had morphed down, now - worn out by the battle. His mask was fully torn off.
			The eyeball made a sickening *plop* noise as it fell out of its socket and landed on the ground below. Connor smacked the socket with his right hand, and screamed in pure physical pain. Then, he was shaken from this by a creaking, groaning noise.
			He looked up, and managed to get out the words, "Oh, fuck."
			Olivia desperately tried to stop it, but she was too bruised - too broken.
			A falling piece of the building landed, crushing him. His body barely held on to life, as his conscious mind faded.

Sparky leapt up, biting down on Junior's chin, his claws swiping wildly at the monster's chest. Chunks of flesh fell to the ground, before Junior jumped in the air and belly-flopped, crushing Sparky's ribs.

			Junior clutched the stump in agony. Connor twirled his blade-arm, and ran forward, before impaling its primary heart.

			Junior screamed out, and howled. Then, its blood red eyes seemed to fade away, leaving eerily humanlike blue eyes in their place.
			Connor stepped forward. He let go of his neck wound, which had now started to close.

			"Help me..."

			"Stay where you are! I'll kill this thing, then I'll help you!" he barked firmly. His own eye lost its red haze, now frantically searching for any nearby child survivors.
			"Please... I'm so cold now... Help me..." the voice said again.
			He looked down.
			No.
			Can't be.
			Another trick.
			Or he was going mad.
			"Help me..." Junior begged again.
			Connor sank to his knees.

			He saw... awful things.
			Cutting. Burning. Injections. So many injections.

			He saw his father Campbell sreaming in fury, as even more super-serum flowed into the boy's body. It seemed they'd drained all the kid's blood, and replaced it with serum. And it seemed Campbell was enraged that his son was a monster, and not a god.
			He felt the pain, the fear, the rage flowing through the kid's head, as he slaughtered through Beslon just moments before, trying desperately to get the pain to stop. The same pain in the skull that tormented Connor.

			"I... Okay, hold on. You're a strong kid, right?" Connor encouraged. "You're gonna be okay. We'll get you to a friend of mine, and you'll survive."
			"No..." Junior cut in. "Help me... to get rid of... the pain..."

			"Didn't want to... Didn't want to hurt anyone..." the poor creature said as his heaved.
			"I know." Connor nodded solemnly.
			"Pain... gonna come back... unless..."
			"No." Connor shook his head. "I'm sorry. I... can't."
			"Please... have to... before..."
			"I'm so sorry..." Connor cried.
			"Want to die... while I'm... still me... Please?"
			Connor took a deep breath, then shuffled closer to his head.
			"Listen..." he whispered, cradling the head gently. "I'm gonna find the men who did this to us. I'm gonna kill every last one of them. And I'm gonna make sure no one ever, *ever* does it again. And I promise, I'll remember you. Til the day I die."
