			"No. Like you really are. With your blue eyes and your brown hair and your freckles." Connor nodded, tears streaming from his eye.
			"Thank... you..."
			Connor stood, and took a deep breath. He held his blade in the air, right above Junior's neck.
			"I'll make it as quick as I can, okay? No more pain, I swear."
			Junior let out a rattling noise - a bloody, ragged breath.
			"Shh..." Connor gently whispered. "Go in peace."
			"I'm... sorry..." Junior rasped. "Your friends... all those people..."
			"I forgive you."
			*SCH-SQUELCH*

			Connor took a few steps out of the crater, as his broken, bladed arm fell off almost lazily - the connective tissue finally annihilated. The whole square was a devastated, scarred landscape. Buildings had been shattered, hundreds of bodies strewn across, and enough blood to feed a vampire for years. He made it to Sparky's body, and pressed his hand against his packmate's head. Still a flicker.

			Connor cracked his head against the stone, but rose anyway.
			"I WAS A *HUMAN!*" he screamed, pouncing into the air and slashing wildly. "I WAS A HUMAN BOY, AND YOU *STOLE THAT FROM ME!* AND THEN YOU *LEFT* ME! BEATEN! BROKEN! *BLEEDING!* YOU TURNED ME INTO A *FUCKING _MONSTER!_*"
			The Commandant's flesh tore under Connor's assault, while Sparky and Trey forced themselves to rise. The hate - the pain that Connor felt - flashed through their skulls too.
			The Commandant was hurt, sure - but he had more than enough left. He slammed his boot into Connor's head, before picking him up and slamming him down against his knee. The crunching sound of his back filled the air, before he tossed the limp, bleeding berserker towards his friends.
			"ABOMINATION!" a voice boomed from the edge of the valley.
			The fighters looked up, and saw it.
			The Judge.
			"Oh, hey buddy." the Commandant grinned. "Seems I've had all the fun, I'm afraid."
			"Oh, the fun has only just begun." the Judge smiled, sliding down.
			"Connor's mine. You can have his friends." the Commandant snarled. "I'm killing him."
			The Judge approached the pile of broken Werewolves, then turned to the Commandant.
			"If you want to kill them..." they growled, drawing their blades, "Then you'll have to go through *me.*"

		Battle of Karelia - Part 1
		______________________________
		SCENE
			"I always knew I couldn't trust you, alien." the Commandant growled. "You and our boss."
			"Likewise, abomination." the Judge snarled back. The two monsters circled each other, like beasts fighting over a kill.
			Connor rose, readying his claws.
			"Down, youngblood." the Judge barked. "This one's head belongs to me."
			"Lucky you, boy." the Commandant hissed. "Take a break while I kill the freak."
			The Judge was done playing. They rushed in, their blade clashing against the Commandant's skin.
			Every cut on the Commandant's body had been delivered by the boys sending their hardest strikes, their strongest slashes.
			This was an opening slice, and red droplets splashed onto the snow.
			The Commandant replied by sending a punch into the Judge's gut. A punch so hard, it shook the air and sent them an inch upwards. Undeterred, the Judge spun in a whirlwind motion, tearing flesh from the Commandant's hide. The two fiends were locked in a fight to the bitter end.

			"Tsentral'nyy, eto Sokolov." Ivan whispered into the radio.
			"Sokolov, this is Bevan. What's your sitrep?"
			"The Judge has arrived... and it's fighting the Commandant."
			A pause.
			"How about our team?" Bevan finally asked.
			"Wounded. Clinging on." Ivan replied. "I'm almost out of ammo."
			"Ivan - save your shots." Chloe cut in. "I've got a plan, and it needs your bullets."
			"Derrington is right." Morozov agreed. "Maintain obs, but do not engage. Keep us in the loop on the fight."
			"Prinyal." Ivan nodded, observing the battle from his scope.

			"DIE, ABOMINATION!" the Judge screamed. Their swords were shattered now - replaced with morphed claws. The Commandant had likewise opted for wrist-blades. Each monster took out chunks of the other.
			The Commandant sent a stab-punch to the Judge's chest, puncturing into their right lung. The Judge, unbothered, struck out at the Commandant's neck, aiming for the jugular.
			Blood sprayed out from both, as they fell backwards, clutching and closing their wounds.
			"I'm gonna kill you, alien filth." the Commandant spat. "There'll be no room for your kind in my new world."
			"I should've realised it sooner." the Judge hissed back. "I should've noticed the lies of the False Lord when he made the likes of *you.*"
			The two charged forward, and slashed. The air stood still for a moment, as both tore past the other. After a second that felt like an hour, a disgusting slipping noise emanated from both.
			The Commandant's hand fell off. As did the Judge's top half.

			"Chloe, I must protest." Bevan pressed, rushing after her.
			"No offence, Major, but you'll need two hands for this." she shook her head, zipping up an NBC suit.
			"None taken. But we have the Giants!" he begged.
			"There's no NBC suits for them. They won't fit in the Kestrel. And we need them here, in case things go sour, to hold off the Commandant while you evacuate." she replied clinically, boarding the VTOL.
			"Ready to deploy?" the pilot asked, seating in the cockpit.
			"Almost." Chloe nodded, strapping herself in. A pair of Giants rushed over, carrying barrels which they loaded into the craft.
			"Chloe..." Bevan began.
			"Major, the man I love is out there. As are two of my best friends. And they could all die if I don't do this." she cut in.
			Bevan sighed deeply. "Be careful."

			The Commandant howled in rage and pain, gripping his arm-stump. His eyes flashed a bright red, the fury cutting through the xeno-endorphins.
			At this, the three Werewolves rose. Catching their breaths, they injected each other with Paradrenaline, and charged to meet the monster.
			The force of their impact shook the snow in the valley, echoing out into the forests above.
			But it just wasn't enough.
			Trey gladly broke his fists against the Commandant's hide, his pain fading as he felt flesh rip around his shattered knuckles. Sparky tore out chunks of meat with such ferocity, his own teeth came loose. Connor drove his claws deep into the Commandant's thigh, hitting an artery and being showered in blood.
			The Commandant didn't break.
			First, he grabbed Trey, and wrapped his hand around the man's neck. Squeezing and shaking, he felt the windpipe crush, before the neck-bones made a sickening snap. Trey's limp body fell down, his face contorting and his teeth gnashing - trying, in vain, to get back up and kill.
			Sparky was the next victim. The Commandant's hand plunged into Sparky's bleeding mouth, and ripped out his tongue. Then, a wristblade shot out, popping out of Sparky's throat. The wolf fell to the ground, hot blood pouring out.
			Finally, he turned his attention to Connor. Slamming him to the ground, he drove his boot into his face.

			The first stomp was almost merciful. By rocking Connor's brain against his skull walls, he lost a little bit of consciousness.
			That made the next hurt a tiny bit less, as his jaw snapped in two.
			Then another stomp. And another. And another. Before long, Connor's entire lower face was a puddle of red mush and bone fragments. His glowing red eyes stared up, ever defiant.
			The Commandant knelt down, and sighed.
			"Such a waste." he spat, before rising his boot up.
			Blood shot out from Connor's lower face - as his lungs desperately tried to make the noise "Fuck you."
			"What was that?" the Commandant gloated. "I can't hear you."
			And then, a noise boomed from the sky. The Kestrel hovered over the reddened valley.
			The Commandant looked up, and chuckled. "Oh no, not a VTOL! However shall I cope?"
			The doors opened, and Chloe pushed down the barrels. The Commandant punched one before it could hit him, and... he screamed.
			A horrific yellowish gas filled his lungs, while clear liquid burned into his skin. More barrels rained down.
			Ivan looked on, and grinned. "Umnaya devochka."
			He fired Isabella at the barrels, and the exploding bullets ripped them open, spewing out their contents into the valley.
			The blood-soaked snowpit became a yellow, misty crater, and the Commandant hacked and spat bile. He stumbled, and fell to his knees.
			His eyes flashed red, he roared, and sprinted off with superhuman speed, uprooting trees as he pushed into the forest.
			"GO! GO! GO!" Chloe barked, as the Kestrel touched down into the valley. She hopped out, as Connor went deathly still.
			"Come on... Come on..." she begged, hoisting him into the craft. She ran over, and did the same for Sparky and Trey.
			Then, she looked down.
			The Judge passed out from the gas and blood loss, but their face was still contorted in hate. The Commandant's severed hand was a pace away.
			She hesitated, but hauled their top half into the craft, and dosed them with xeno-endorphins, ensuring they stayed unconscious. She threw the hand in, and pulled the door shut. The Kestrel tore off into the sky, while Ivan rose up, and began the slow walk back to the labs.

		Battle of Karelia - Part 2
		______________________________
		SCENE
			Connor woke from his healing coma, launching a globule of blood and bile from his face. He snapped up, and looked around frantically. Immediately, he spotted his friends, and relaxed.
			"You're okay, you're okay." Chloe rushed over.
			Trey came too. He had morphed a neck-brace, and was still in his costume - minus the mask. Sparky dragged himself over, his mouth still toothless and torn.
			Connor tried to speak, but only made a hissing, rasping noise. He touched his mouth, and... no he didn't. There was no mouth.
			Chloe grabbed a glass, and handed it over. Connor looked at his reflection.
			Calling it a 'face' was incredibly generous. Everything from the nose down had been smashed into an unrecognisable mush. Cracks and bruises adorned the top half of his head. Fresh bone-pulp was forming around the edges of his head, developing into embryonic jawbones.
			He grabbed his packmates' shoulders, and closed his eyes, pressing his mind into them.
			"Where are we?" he thought.
			"Back in that KGB lab." Trey explained. "That 'Commandant' bloke managed to escape, but we're alive at least."
			"I only just woke up, too." Sparky thought. "That monster hurt our mouths really badly."
			"How are you doing?" Connor asked Trey.
			"I'm fine. Chloe re-set my neck. Still feel like shit, but nowhere near as bad as you guys."
			Connor thought for a moment, and morphed. The black tar poured out of his skin and formed around his 'face,' forming a prosthetic jaw.
			"Nice." Trey grinned. "Don't think she'll be kissing you for a little while, though."
			Chloe chuckled, and wrapped her arms around him. He smiled warmly, resting his head against hers.
			"That thing was..." she began, lost for words.
			"He could've killed Junior in five minutes flat." Connor grimaced. His words were slurred from the crudeness of his jaw.
			"No kidding. The three of us, *plus* the Judge?" Trey shuddered.
			"I hate him. I wish I could hate him to death!" Sparky barked.
			"I got his hand." Chloe nodded. "I'll take a look as soon as we get back to Drackhill."
			"Did we kill him?" asked Connor.
			Chloe sighed, and squeezed him tightly. "I'm so sorry... I thought the gas would at least incapacitate him. He escaped."
			"Don't be sorry, you did the right thing." Connor said trying and failing to animate a smile. "You saved our lives. What happened to the Judge?"
			"They're downstairs." Sparky answered. "Locked up, with more of that stinky gas ready to go if they try anything."
			Connor chuckled, and stood. His whole body ached, but he didn't care.
			"I wanna see them." he said, his words slurred.
			"Why?" asked Sparky.
			"The Judge wants the Commandant dead, same as us. And they want it for a reason. I wanna know why. And to do that... I'm gonna have to ask them."
			The group headed downwards, into the facility.

			Chloe cautiously approached the blast-proof screen. Behind it, the Judge - or rather, their top half - was reclined on a hospital bed. Barrels of toxic gas surrounded them, with remote-detonated charges fixed to the bases, ready to coat the room in chlorine should the Judge opt for a repeat incident. Stubby little legs poked out from their abdomen.
			She leaned into the microphone.
			"Can you hear me?" she asked.
			"Leave me, human." they replied. "Let me rest."
			"I want some answers, first." she said coldly. "I bet you're hungry, right? Regrowing your entire bottom half... Maybe you answer my questions, and I get you some food."
			"Maybe I let myself starve, and you get no answer at all." the Judge grinned.
			"Why'd you save the others? Why did you attack the Commandant?" she asked.
			Silence.
			"Okay, have it your way." she sighed. "I just got the vibe that you were some honourable warrior."
			"Do not *dare* question my honour, human." the Judge snapped.
			"Oh." Chloe chuckled. "Did I hit a nerve?"
			The Judge's lip curled, and they shuffled to sit up on their waist.
			"I attacked the Abomination, because I want it to die." they finally said. "The life or death of the youngbloods was of no consequence to me."
			"Then why didn't you wait until they'd died? They could've hurt him more. You could've had a better chance at killing him."
			"I will not explain myself to a human. I will not debase my thoughts by speaking them in your tongues." they snarled.
			"Fine. Tell me about yourself, then." she shrugged. "What's your name?"
			"I am the Judge. 'Kakhral' in my tongue. Supreme Ashkat-Narud of the 12th Legion. Vanquisher of the Daelach Heresy. Conqueror of Zaklat V. A thousand Thraxi died screaming but some of these titles - I can go on."
			"Kakhral. Is that your name, then?" Chloe asked, thoroughly unimpressed.
			"It is my purpose."
			"Your people don't have names?"
			The Judge paused. "My... my people have no need of them."
			"Why not?"
			"We are soldiers." they finally answered. "Tools. Weapons. Bullets, even. Giving us a name is as logical as giving your gun a name."
			"Shh, it's okay. Don't cry." Ivan whispered to Isabella, grinning as he stroked the rifle. Chloe stifled a chuckle.
			"Do you have a name?" the Judge asked.
			"My name is Chloe. Chloe Derrington." she replied.
			"Ah. You killed me." they nodded.
			"I just cooked up the endorphins." she shrugged.
			"Indeed you did, Chloe-Chloederrington."
			"That's--" she began, before stopping herself.
			"Nekh-shar, morai. Thrax-shar, xel." they said, like a quote.
			"Can you translate that, please?" she asked.
			"In faith, strength. In heresy, weakness." Trey cut in. "I... I don't know why I know that."
			"Ah, youngbloods." the Judge smiled. "And you - the freshest of the pack."
			"What did you mean by that?" asked Chloe.
			"That was what the Uunadari told us. But it was not heresy that made me weak - it was the venom you cut into my hide. A lie."
			"Uunadari?" Trey tilted his head. "I can't get an exact translation. Preachers?"
			"I got 'Prophets.'" Connor shrugged.
			"Yes..." the Judge growled. "But now, I see they were liars. The poisons of Chloe-Chloederrington is but one proof. Your blade liberated more than my head from my shoulders - mine eyes have been opened."
			"Why are you on Earth?" Chloe cut in.
			"I was sent here by the Uunadari to await the arrival of the Great One. And I thought I had found them."
			"Who did you think you found?"
			"The Lord." the Judge nodded. "I swore my fealty to them."
			"Who's the Lord?" Chloe pressed.
			"They are the Lord." the Judge shrugged. "They never saw fit to tell me more."
			Connor timidly approached the screen, looking the Judge in the eyes.
			"Where did you come from?"
			"From the stars, youngblood." the Judge smiled, almost warmly.
			"Tell me about your people. Please."
			The Judge sighed. "I have no people. I am a Golgothan - we are vat-grown from genetic templates."
			"Clones?" Chloe tilted her head. "You're clones?"
			"Yes. We are produced by the Makers for war."
			"Makers?" Trey pressed. "Someone made us?"
			"Not *you,* youngblood. My Makers were a different being. The Golgothan Legions were created by the Conclave - uplifted from base animals into warriors."
			The Judge closed their eyes for a moment, letting nostalgia wash over them.
			"My earliest memories are of being deployed to quash the rebellions of Zaklat V. Its people had betrayed the Empire, and so my Legion descended upon them, and sent their soldiers' souls to the King of Graves."
			"Empire?" Trey cocked an eyebrow. "Is that why you're here on Earth? To conquer us?"
			"I came here in sacred duty." the Judge shook their head. "The Empire lies far away, beyond the Veil. Your world is safe from us as long as it stands."
			"The Veil?" Chloe asked.
			"A barrier of dark energy that makes reliable travel impossible." they explained clinically. "The Uunadari believed that beyond it lies an avatar of the Great One."
			"So, you're not just a soldier. You're special forces. On a solo mission." Ivan noted. "Are all your people like you?"
			"How observant, halfbreed." the Judge grinned. "No. The Golgothans are the greatest army in the galaxy. But we - myself and the youngbloods - are more than our host races. We are Moxidari."
			"What's that?" asked Connor. "I can't make out the word."
			"Your tongues are not advanced enough for it." they shrugged. "The Moxidari are the Moxidari. There is no other term."
			"Is 'Moxidari' your word for people who were given the Serum before birth?" asked Chloe.
			"Yes." the Judge nodded. "It was applied across my entire batch. Only I survived."
			"But you're all identical?" Chloe titled her head. "And you're all vat-grown? The circumstances of your gestation would be identical, no?"
			"Such is the mystery of the Moxidari." the Judge shrugged. "I am not a scholar, Chloe-Chloederrington. I cannot answer all your questions."
			"Maybe you can answer mine." Connor began. He placed his hand against the glass.
			"What are you doing?" Chloe whispered. The Judge placed their own hand up to Connor's.
			Even through the glass, the two Moxidari could join their minds together. Such a merge was far from the wholesome union of comrades he had felt with Sparky and Trey. Instead... he saw into the mind of a soldier, born for war.
			He felt the recoil of a magnetic rifle as it punched through enemy lines. He felt the lashes of pain as Uunadari delivered flaggelation after flaggelation. He felt the Judge's ship crash into the Earth, and he felt the moment the Judge re-awoke from stasis - and the moment they drove their blades through Connor's chest.
			He looked up, and saw the False Lord. An old white man, with slicked-back hair, a cropped beard, and an impeccable suit. His violet eyes shone, and he felt the Judge genuflect.
			Finally, both pulled back.
			"Why?" Connor asked. "Why save us?"
			The Judge looked away. "I... I saw nothing."
			"What do you mean?" Chloe pressed.
			"I was raised in the Faith." they began. "I was always told - the faithful servants of the Great One will sit at their table in death. I have always been a faithful servant. But when I died... I saw nothing. No table. No glory. No Great One. All I could perceive was pain."
			"So that's what it was? A crisis of faith?" asked Connor.
			"A betrayal. By the Uunadari, by the Great One, by the False Lord... and so I responded in kind. If the Great One shall not embrace me, then I shall turn away from their light."
			A tense silence filled the room.
			"I have said all I wish to." the Judge began. "Please, leave me."
			"Let's go." Connor nodded to the others. They followed him to a private segment of the laboratory.

		Karelia - Aftermath
		______________________________
		SCENE
			"What did you see?" asked Chloe.
			"I'm not sure." Connor admitted. "There was a human - some aristo, by the looks of it - who the Judge *thought* was their messiah. They were an Esper - that's for sure."
			"Who were they?" Trey tilted his head.
			"No idea. I guess a mix of being from another species, and being from one where you're all identical, makes facial recognition quite hard. The Judge didn't remember anything we'd find identifiable, so I couldn't see it."
			"The real question is... what do we do with them?" Bevan said, rubbing his eye.
			"We can't trust them." Chloe shook her head.
			"They saved our lives." Trey countered.
			"They tried to kill us." Sparky cut in.
			"We share an enemy." Bevan sighed.
			"You're not seriously suggesting that we *ally* with that... that *thing?*" Ivan pulled his head back.
			"I don't know if we can trust them or not." Connor said finally. "But I do know that when they spoke to us just now, they weren't lying."
			"I felt that too." Trey nodded. "This... telepathy thingy, it's weird. But I could tell they were telling the truth."
			"Me too." Sparky concurred. "But just because they're being honest doesn't change what they did!"
